docs.title: scMultiBench
docs.text:
A benchmark of single-cell multimodal integration methods. Run 36 methods through one Python API, score them with scIB metrics, and compare them in bubble tables and rankings. 

pip install multibench-sc

Get started How it works

docs.title: API reference
docs.text: The package is imported as import multibench as mtb. The tables below list every public function by step; each name links to its reference entry (signature, parameters, examples).

docs.title: The five layers
docs.text:
A benchmark run has five steps: discover a method, prepare the data, run, score, compare.

import multibench as mtb

mtb.find_methods(category="vertical", modalities=["rna", "adt"])          # 1. discover
mtb.io.export_dataset(mdata, "data/MYCITE", rna="rna", adt="adt",
                      labels="rna:celltype")                               # 2. prepare
batch = mtb.run_all("MYCITE", "vertical", out_dir="runs/MYCITE",
                    data_path="data")                                      # 3. run (+ score)
res = mtb.run("Matilda", "vertical", out_dir="runs/Matilda",
              inputs=mtb.inputs_for("MYCITE", "vertical", "Matilda",
                                    data_path="data"))                     #    ... or one method
scores = mtb.evaluate(res.output,
                      labels=mtb.labels_for("MYCITE", "vertical", "Matilda",
                                            data_path="data"))             # 4. score
stored = mtb.load_results("vertical", dataset="D11")                       # 5. compare
mtb.plot.bubble(stored)
Details

Your rows next to the stored ones. mtb.to_long turns the scores into the long frame that mtb.load_results returns, so both can be concatenated and drawn with mtb.plot.bubble.

Same Leiden backend. Set mtb.config.DEFAULT.leiden_flavor = "leidenalg" before mtb.evaluate so your ARI, NMI and iF1 use the backend of the published tables.

docs.title: 1. Discover
docs.text:
Which methods exist, what each needs, how to cite it. Nothing is downloaded.

entry point what it does mtb.list_methods Method ids, optionally for one category. mtb.find_methods Method ids matching every filter given (category, task, modalities, ...). mtb.method_info Everything the registry holds on one method: environment, variants, runtime, GPU needs, reference. mtb.params_for The hyperparameters a method variant accepts, with their defaults. mtb.describe_layout How to lay out your own dataset folder for a category. mtb.cite Citation text or BibTeX for the benchmark and the methods you ran. mtb.list_tasks The valid task values. mtb.list_categories The valid category values, each with a short description.

docs.title: 2. Prepare data
docs.text:
Put your matrices into a dataset folder and find the files a method reads.

entry point what it does mtb.io.export_dataset Write an AnnData / MuData (or loose matrices) as a dataset folder. mtb.io.to_canonical Convert one matrix to the canonical .h5 (features x cells). mtb.io.read_canonical Read a canonical .h5 back as an AnnData (cells x features). mtb.io.normalize_peak_names Write a copy of a canonical .h5 with ATAC peak names spelled the way the methods expect. mtb.inputs_for {role: path} of the files a method variant reads from a dataset folder. mtb.labels_for {name: path} of a dataset's cell-type label CSVs; with category and method, in the order that method stacks its cells. mtb.data.fetch Download the named reference datasets unless they are already present. mtb.data.fetch_outputs Download precomputed run_all outputs for a tutorial dataset. mtb.data.fetchable The dataset ids fetch can download.

docs.title: 3. Run
docs.text:
Run methods in their environments. mtb.scan shows what can run before you start.

entry point what it does mtb.scan Which methods can run on a dataset, why the others cannot, and the command each would run. mtb.run Run one method and load its output (a RunResult). mtb.run_all Run and score every applicable method; returns a BatchResult. mtb.sweep Run one method over a range of one hyperparameter. mtb.load_batch Reload a saved BatchResult. mtb.BatchResult What run_all returns: a summary table, a long frame, a figure, rescoring. mtb.env.status Which method environments are installed on this machine. mtb.env.plan Which environments a set of methods needs, with download and disk sizes. mtb.env.install Install those environments; a dry run until dry_run=False. mtb.env.doctor What is installed, what is missing, and the install command for the gaps. mtb.env.recipe The build recipe of one method's environment.

docs.title: 4. Score
docs.text:
Compute scIB metrics for a run output.

entry point what it does mtb.evaluate scIB metrics of a run output against cell-type labels (and batch labels). mtb.to_long Reshape evaluate's result into the long results frame.

docs.title: 5. Compare
docs.text:
Load the stored metric tables, rank methods and draw figures.

entry point what it does mtb.load_results The stored metric tables as one long frame. mtb.available_datasets Dataset ids with stored results. mtb.results_coverage Which (category, dataset, method) combinations have results, and from which source. mtb.recommend Rank methods for a category from the stored results, with coverage shown. mtb.DegenerateRerunWarning Warning class for a re-run row that most likely failed silently. mtb.plot.bubble Bubble table of a long results frame. mtb.plot.bar Each method's overall score across datasets, as bars. mtb.plot.build_table The numbers behind a bubble table, without drawing it. mtb.plot.BubbleTable What build_table returns: per-family matrices, ranks and row order. mtb.catalog.methods The methods table as a DataFrame. mtb.catalog.datasets The datasets table, including which datasets have stored results. mtb.catalog.metrics The metrics table, with a description of each metric. mtb.catalog.canonical_id The canonical method id for any known spelling. mtb.catalog.canonical_metric The canonical metric code for any known spelling ("ari" -> "ARI"). mtb.catalog.known_metrics The metric codes, in family order.

docs.title: Configuration and errors
docs.text:
The environment variables are listed on the config page.

entry point what it does mtb.config.Config Paths and settings (data_path, envs_dir, leiden_flavor); every function reads mtb.config.DEFAULT. mtb.AmbiguousVariantError Raised when a method has several variants and neither modalities= nor the dataset's files select one.

docs.title: The same story from the shell
docs.text:
Each multibench subcommand wraps one Python function and takes the same argument names. multibench <command> --help lists the flags.

terminal
multibench layout vertical                         # how to lay out your data
multibench convert my.h5ad data/MYCITE --rna X --adt obsm:protein --labels obs:celltype
multibench scan MYCITE --category vertical --data-path data
multibench params Matilda                          # the hyperparameters --param accepts
multibench run --method Matilda --category vertical --out-dir runs/Matilda \
    --input rna=data/MYCITE/rna.h5 --input adt=data/MYCITE/adt.h5 --input cty=data/MYCITE/cty.csv
multibench evaluate --output runs/Matilda/embedding.h5 --labels data/MYCITE/cty.csv \
    --method Matilda --dataset MYCITE --category vertical --out runs/Matilda/long.csv
multibench run-all MYCITE --category vertical --data-path data --out-dir runs/MYCITE
multibench plot bubble --input runs/MYCITE --out mine.pdf               # your runs
multibench plot bubble --category vertical --dataset D11 --out d11.pdf   # a stored table
multibench cite Matilda MOFA2
Details

Output. Tables, ids and commands go to stdout. Progress, warnings and errors go to stderr, so 2>/dev/null hides them.

Full tables. scan and run-all --dry-run clip long text to 80 characters. --columns all or --format csv|tsv|json prints every column in full, including command.

Dry run. run --dry-run prints the command without running it.

Hyperparameters. params METHOD lists them per variant. Set one with --param KEY=VALUE on run, or --param METHOD:KEY=VALUE on run-all.

Metrics. evaluate --metrics takes a family (clustering, batch, all) or a comma-separated list of codes.

Overlay. plot --input together with --category adds your rows to the stored table. --dataset filters both, so your rows must be for a dataset the stored table has.

Leiden backend. multibench evaluate uses the default igraph backend, not the leidenalg backend of the published tables, and has no option to change it. To match them, score in Python with leiden_flavor = "leidenalg".

ATAC data. Pass --category to convert so the ATAC file gets the name that category expects.

Environments. The env commands are dry runs until --run.

Exit codes. 0 success, 1 runtime error (MULTIBENCH_DEBUG=1 prints the traceback), 2 usage error.

docs.title: Errors and warnings
docs.text:
An invalid argument raises a standard exception whose message names the valid values or the fix.

Details
  • KeyError: unknown method id, with a did-you-mean hint.
  • ValueError: unknown category, task, atac or modality token; the message lists the valid values.
  • TypeError: a single string where a list is expected (methods="StabMap"); the message shows the list form.
  • FileNotFoundError: missing dataset folder or file; the message lists the folders that exist, or the path and the working directory.
  • mtb.AmbiguousVariantError: a method with several variants that neither modalities= nor the dataset's files select. It is a ValueError and also a KeyError.
  • OSError: the method's environment is not installed; the message names the install command.

Warnings are UserWarnings. The one for a re-run row that most likely failed silently is mtb.DegenerateRerunWarning, so you can filter on it.

docs.title: The metrics= vocabulary
docs.text:
evaluate, load_results, recommend and BatchResult.rescore take the same selector: "clustering", "batch", "all", or a list of metric codes such as ["ARI", "NMI"].

Details

Families.

  • "clustering": ARI, NMI, ASW, iASW, iF1, cLISI (mtb.plot.CLUSTERING_METRICS).
  • "batch": ASW_batch, GC, iLISI, kBET (mtb.plot.BATCH_METRICS).
  • "all": both families; evaluate then needs batch labels.

Default (None). evaluate computes the clustering family, plus the batch family when batch labels are available. load_results keeps every metric; recommend ranks on the clustering family.

kBET. evaluate computes kBET only when it is named in a list.

Errors. A single code still goes in a list (metrics=["ARI"]). A task name or an unknown code raises ValueError listing the valid values.

Leiden backend. ARI, NMI and iF1 use a Leiden clustering sweep whose backend is mtb.config.DEFAULT.leiden_flavor: "igraph" (default, faster) or "leidenalg" (the backend of the published tables). The two can differ by up to about 0.1 ARI on the same embedding. Score the runs you compare with the same backend.

Older scanpy. With scanpy older than 1.10, leidenalg is used.

docs.title: Method environments
docs.text:
Each method runs in a linux-64 environment, shared with compatible methods (mtb.method_info(m)["env"]), installed with mtb.env.install. On macOS and Windows only the dry run works; a real install refuses unless force=True (--force).

Details

Method scripts. The upstream scripts run unmodified. The package builds the command, converts the inputs and loads the output.

docs.title: Run modes: prefix and conda
docs.text:
mtb.run activates an installed environment directly from its folder under envs_dir (prefix mode, no conda needed), or falls back to conda run -n <env> (conda mode). MULTIBENCH_RUN_MODE=conda|prefix forces one.

Details

Prefix mode. The command runs as bash -c '<activate>; exec "$@"' -- <cmd>. <activate> sets CONDA_PREFIX, CONDA_DEFAULT_ENV and PATH, and sources the environment's etc/conda/activate.d/*.sh scripts.

Forced prefix mode with no environment folder on disk raises OSError.

Custom wrapper. cmd_template= on mtb.run replaces both modes.

Installed or not. mtb.env.env_prefix returns the folder mtb.run would activate, or None. mtb.scan's env_ok column uses the same test.

docs.title: Archive flavours: cpu and gpu
docs.text:
Five torch environments have a CUDA build and a smaller CPU-only build. mtb.env.install picks the CPU build when mtb.env.host_has_gpu finds no NVIDIA GPU.

Details

Which environments. env_sciPENN, matilda, scmb_scjoint, scmb_torch, scmb_scmm2.

Choosing a build. flavor="cpu" or flavor="gpu" (--flavor on the CLI) overrides the default "auto".

Same name either way. Both builds install under the environment's own name, so mtb.run and mtb.scan need no change. mtb.env.status() reports the installed build as flavor.

docs.title: GPU or CPU?
docs.text:
Six methods need an NVIDIA GPU (mtb.method_info(m)["requires_gpu"]). Without one, mtb.run raises OSError before starting and mtb.scan gives the reason. The other methods run without a GPU.

Details

GPU-only methods. scBridge, moETM, SMILE, sciCAN, UnitedNet, iPOLNG.

CPU switches. For scripts that use CUDA by default, method_info(m)["cpu_params"] holds the values that turn it off (scJoint use_cuda='', scMDC device='cpu'). Without a GPU, mtb.run adds them unless you set the key yourself; run(..., dry_run=True) shows the command.

Always on CPU. scMM, scMVP and scMSI run on CPU, also on a GPU host.

docs.title: RunResult
docs.text:
mtb.run returns a RunResult. Its output is the method's primary output (for example the embedding), ready for mtb.evaluate.

Details

Fields.

  • method: the method id.
  • out_dir: the working directory of the run.
  • cmd: the full command that ran, including the environment wrapper.
  • output: the primary output, loaded. An embedding may be dims x cells; evaluate re-orients it.
  • extra: {file: loaded output} for the method's extra outputs.
  • stdout, stderr: the captured streams.

Failures. A non-zero exit raises RuntimeError with the end of the output. A missing environment raises OSError before anything is written; on a host with no environment and no conda, the run fails with FileNotFoundError for conda instead.

docs.title: Version
docs.text: mtb.__version__ is the installed version.

docs.title: Deprecated in 0.3.0
docs.text:
Renamed 0.2.1 spellings still work in 0.3.x with a DeprecationWarning and will be removed in 0.4. Removed ones raise an error.

Details: renamed (still work until 0.4) 0.2.1 0.3.0 mtb.plan(dataset, category, ...) mtb.scan(dataset, category, ...) - the same frame, command column included mtb.plan_commands(...) mtb.scan(...) mtb.runtime_hint(m) mtb.method_info(m)["runtime"] mtb.plot.plot_bubble(...) mtb.plot.bubble(...) evaluate(..., task="clustering" / "batch" / "all") evaluate(..., metrics="clustering" / "batch" / "all") evaluate(..., family=...) evaluate(..., metrics=<token>) evaluate(..., only=[...]) evaluate(..., metrics=[...]) load_results(..., method=...) load_results(..., methods=...) load_results(..., metric=[...]) load_results(..., metrics=[...]) load_results(..., task=... / family=...) load_results(..., metrics=<token>) recommend(..., task=... / family=...) recommend(..., metrics=<token>) multibench evaluate --only A,B multibench evaluate --metrics A,B (stderr: warning: --only is deprecated since 0.3.0; use --metrics)

Mixing. Passing metrics= together with a deprecated selector raises TypeError (evaluate() got metrics= together with the deprecated ['task']; pass metrics= only).

Finding old spellings. python -W error::DeprecationWarning turns the warnings into errors.

Details: removed removed error mtb.command_preview(...) AttributeError - use mtb.run(..., dry_run=True) mtb.io.from_mudata(...) AttributeError - mtb.io.export_dataset(mdata, ..., rna="rna", atac="atac", labels="rna:celltype") mtb.io.write_labels(...) AttributeError - export_dataset writes the label files; by hand: pd.Series(labels, name="x").to_csv(path, index=False) list_methods(task=...) / (runnable=...) TypeError: list_methods() only takes category since 0.3.0; task=... are find_methods filters - use find_methods(category, task=...) find_methods("vertical", "clustering") (positional filters) TypeError: find_methods() takes from 0 to 1 positional arguments but 2 were given method_info(m, files_dir=...) TypeError: method_info() got an unexpected keyword argument 'files_dir' - the catalog columns are mtb.catalog.methods() cite(methods=[...]) TypeError: cite() got an unexpected keyword argument 'methods' - cite([...]) or one id per argument cite([ids], "bibtex") TypeError: cite(): method ids must be strings, got list; pass ONE list (cite(['Matilda', 'MOFA2'])) or one id per argument - fmt= is keyword-only inputs_for(dataset, method, category) TypeError: inputs_for argument order is (dataset, category, method) since 0.3.0; you passed (dataset, method, category) labels_for(dataset, method, category) TypeError: labels_for argument order is (dataset, category, method) since 0.3.0; you passed (dataset, method, category) labels_for(dataset, "<data_path>") TypeError: labels_for: pass data_path= by keyword; the 2nd positional argument is category since 0.3.0 (order: (dataset, category, method)) inputs_for(..., ["rna", "adt"]) (positional modalities) TypeError: inputs_for() takes 3 positional arguments but 4 were given scan(dataset, category, data_path) (positional) TypeError: scan() takes from 1 to 2 positional arguments but 3 were given run(method, category, "clustering", ...) (positional task) TypeError: run() takes 2 positional arguments but 3 positional arguments (and 2 keyword-only arguments) were given run_all(dataset, category) without out_dir TypeError: run_all() needs out_dir= for a real run (dry_run=True returns the scan frame without one) BatchResult.rescore(only=...) TypeError: BatchResult.rescore() got an unexpected keyword argument 'only' - metrics= evaluate(output, category, ...) (positional category) TypeError: evaluate() got multiple values for argument 'labels' - labels is the second positional, the rest keyword-only evaluate(..., slow_metrics=True) TypeError: evaluate() got slow_metrics=, removed in 0.3.0: pass metrics=[...] without cLISI/iLISI (kBET is computed only when it is named in that list) evaluate(..., column="x") TypeError: evaluate() got column=, removed in 0.3.0: pass the Series/column itself as labels= / batch= / clustering= evaluate(..., metric_set="scib") TypeError: evaluate() got metric_set=, removed in 0.3.0: only the scIB metric set exists - drop the argument to_long(df, method, dataset, category) (positional) TypeError: to_long() takes 1 positional argument but 4 were given to_long(..., needs_labels=True) TypeError: to_long() got an unexpected keyword argument 'needs_labels' - add the column to the frame load_results(category, "clustering") (positional) TypeError: load_results() takes from 0 to 1 positional arguments but 2 were given load_results(..., metric_set="scib") TypeError: load_results() got metric_set=, removed in 0.3.0: only the scIB metric set exists - drop the argument available_datasets(..., metric_set=... / clustering=...) TypeError: available_datasets() got an unexpected keyword argument 'metric_set' (likewise 'clustering') mtb.config.category_folder / metric_set_dir, mtb.plot.render / FamilyBlock, mtb.env.group_for and the other mtb.env helpers still importable, but out of __all__ and hidden from dir() - internal

docs.title: Citation
docs.text:
Cite the scMultiBench paper, and the publication of each integration method you run. mtb.cite prints both:

import multibench as mtb

print(mtb.cite("Matilda", "MOFA2"))                # the benchmark, then one line per method
print(mtb.cite(batch.summary.method, fmt="bibtex"))  # every method of batch = mtb.run_all(...), as BibTeX
terminal
multibench cite Matilda MOFA2 --format bibtex --out refs.bib

docs.title: The paper
docs.text:
Liu C, Ding S, Kim HJ, Long S, Xiao D, Ghazanfar S, Yang P. Multitask benchmarking of single-cell multimodal omics integration methods. Nature Methods, 22, 2449–2460 (2025). https://doi.org/10.1038/s41592-025-02856-3

scmultibench.bib (= mtb.cite(fmt='bibtex'))
@article{scMultiBench_2025,
  author = {Liu C and Ding S and Kim HJ and Long S and Xiao D and Ghazanfar S and Yang P},
  title = {Multitask benchmarking of single-cell multimodal omics integration methods},
  journal = {Nature Methods},

}

docs.title: Source code
docs.text:
• Benchmark and method scripts: https://github.com/PYangLab/scMultiBench
  • multibench API (this documentation, the tutorials, PyPI releases): https://github.com/DSichang/scMultiBench, a fork of the repository above

To cite the software, set version and year to the release you used (multibench.__version__).

software.bib
@software{scmultibench_code,
  author    = {Liu, Chunlei and Ding, Sichang and Yang, Pengyi},
  title     = {{scMultiBench}: a benchmark and Python API for single-cell
               multimodal omics integration},
  url       = {https://github.com/PYangLab/scMultiBench},
  note      = {multibench Python package, https://github.com/DSichang/scMultiBench},
  version   = {0.3.1},
  year      = {2025}
}
Details: reporting a run

What to record. The package version (multibench.__version__), each method's environment, and the command it ran (RunResult.cmd).

run_all records. run_all saves one record per method under out_dir, with its environment, parameters and package version.

Stored tables. Frames of re-run results carry the package version of the re-run in frame.attrs["rerun_version"].

  • Running methods and reading metrics: the tutorials for vertical, diagonal, mosaic and cross integration.

docs.title: cLISI / iLISI are NaN on my Mac
docs.text: Install a C++ compiler (on macOS: xcode-select --install), then run evaluate again in a new Python session. See Troubleshooting.

docs.title: env install --run refuses on macOS / Windows
docs.text:
The method environments are linux-64, so run methods on a Linux host. Everything else works on any platform: the registry, the stored results, scan's file check, evaluate and the figures. See Method environments.

Details

Override. --force (force=True in Python) attempts the install anyway.

docs.title: Installation
docs.text:
pip install multibench-sc installs the API on Linux or macOS, Python 3.9 or newer. Running a method also needs that method's environment, which is Linux-only and installed separately.

TL;DR

conda create -n multibench python=3.11 -y && conda activate multibench
pip install multibench-sc
python -c "import multibench as mtb; print(mtb.__version__)"

docs.title: Step 1, Create an isolated environment
docs.text:
Any fresh Python 3.9+ environment works. Conda is optional: the method environments install without it.

Conda (recommended)Mamba (faster solver)venv terminal
conda create -n multibench python=3.11 -y
conda activate multibench
terminal
mamba create -n multibench python=3.11 -y
mamba activate multibench
terminal
python3.11 -m venv .venv
source .venv/bin/activate

docs.title: Step 2, Install multibench
docs.text:
terminal
pip install multibench-sc
Details

Dependencies. The install brings numpy, pandas, h5py, anndata, matplotlib, pyyaml, scanpy and scib. PyTorch, R and the method packages are not installed here; they live in each method's environment.

Developer install. Clone the repository only to edit the notebooks or run the test suite:

terminal
git clone https://github.com/DSichang/scMultiBench.git
cd scMultiBench
pip install -e ".[dev]" --config-settings editable_mode=compat

docs.title: Step 3, Verify the install
docs.text:
terminal
python -c "import multibench as mtb; print(mtb.__version__)"

These calls need no method environment:

import multibench as mtb

print(mtb.list_tasks())
print(mtb.list_methods(category="vertical"))
print(mtb.describe_layout("vertical"))   # how to lay out your own dataset

docs.title: Method environments
docs.text:
Each method runs in its own Linux environment, because the methods' dependencies conflict. Install only the ones you need; --packed downloads prebuilt archives. No conda binary is needed for the packed path.

terminal
multibench env doctor                                      # installed or missing, with the install line
multibench env plan --category vertical                    # environments a category needs, with sizes
multibench env install --methods SCALEX --packed --run     # one method
multibench env install --category vertical --packed --run  # one category
Details

Where they go. mtb.config.DEFAULT.envs_dir: $MULTIBENCH_ENVS_DIR when set, else the envs directory of the conda or mamba on PATH, else ~/.cache/multibench/envs.

Without --packed. The environment is built from its lockfile, which needs conda or mamba and takes longer. A failed archive download also falls back to this build.

CPU and GPU builds. On a host without an NVIDIA GPU, --packed installs the smaller CPU build of the PyTorch environments that have one. --flavor cpu or --flavor gpu overrides the choice.

macOS and Windows. env install --run refuses unless you pass --force; dry runs work. The stored results, scan, evaluate and the plots work on any OS.

Sizes. Categories share environments, so two categories cost less than the sum of their env plan totals. ? disk means the size on disk is not measured yet, so the disk total is a lower bound.

Resuming. env install skips environments that already exist, so rerunning it resumes an interrupted install. With no --methods or --category it installs all 26; run multibench env plan first to see the total.

From Python. mtb.env.status, plan, install, doctor and recipe mirror the CLI; mtb.env.install is a dry run until dry_run=False (reference).

Method scripts. The first mtb.run clones the method scripts (PYangLab/scMultiBench) with git into mtb.config.DEFAULT.repo_path (~/.cache/multibench/scMultiBench_ref after pip install). On a host without network or git, copy a clone of that repository there, or pass its path as repo_path=.

Custom launch. mtb.run(..., cmd_template=...) (--runner on the command line) replaces how the command is launched, for example with a container wrapper.

Preview a run. --dry-run prints the command a run would execute, without running it:

terminal
multibench run --method SCALEX --category diagonal \
    --input rna=<data_path>/D28/rna.h5 --input atac_gas=<data_path>/D28/atac_gas.h5 \
    --out-dir runs/scalex_d28 --dry-run

docs.title: Google Colab
docs.text:
The category tutorials open in Colab from their badge and run on the free CPU runtime. By default (INSTALL_ENVS = False) nothing is downloaded and the method cells use stored outputs; INSTALL_ENVS = True installs the environments and runs the methods.

Details

Default. Run all is safe: the run cells load the benchmark's stored outputs for the dataset, so evaluate scores real embeddings. Offline, the package's stored metric table is used instead, and a printed line says so.

Running methods. INSTALL_ENVS = True needs Colab or a Linux host; on macOS the environment install refuses.

GPU runtime. Choose one before setting the flag (Runtime -> Change runtime type -> T4 GPU). On a CPU runtime the CPU builds are installed and training methods run much slower.

Download per tutorial. GPU builds: cross 3.0 GB, diagonal 5.1 GB, mosaic 5.5 GB, vertical 6.2 GB. CPU builds: cross 1.4 GB, diagonal 1.6 GB, mosaic 1.8 GB, vertical 1.5 GB.

docs.title: Get the data
docs.text:
Each tutorial downloads its dataset on first run. Datasets go to mtb.config.DEFAULT.data_path: ~/.cache/multibench/data after pip install, <repo>/data in a developer install.

import multibench as mtb

mtb.data.fetchable()      # ['D11', 'D28', 'D45', 'D46', 'D52']
mtb.data.fetch("D11")     # no-op when already present
Details

Sizes. D11 (vertical) 11 MB, D28 (diagonal) 137 MB, D45 (mosaic) 290 MB, D46 (mosaic) 97 MB, D52 (cross) 179 MB.

Cache location. When XDG_CACHE_HOME is set, the pip-install data path is $XDG_CACHE_HOME/multibench/data.

Manual download, for example D11:

terminal
DATA=$(python -c 'import multibench as mtb; print(mtb.config.DEFAULT.data_path)')
mkdir -p "$DATA" && wget -qO- https://github.com/DSichang/scMultiBench/releases/download/data-v1/D11.tar.gz | tar xz -C "$DATA"

Other datasets. The full collection of processed datasets is linked from the scMultiBench README. Unpack a dataset under the data path, or anywhere else and pass data_path= (--data-path on the command line). dataset is the folder name; data_path is the folder that contains it.

docs.title: Upgrading from 0.2.1
docs.text: 0.3 renamed a few functions and merged the metric selectors into one metrics= argument. Some old spellings still work in 0.3 with a DeprecationWarning; others were removed and raise an error. The old -> new table is in the API reference.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text:
OSError: conda env '<env>' (<method>) is not installed

The method's environment is missing. Run the install command the message names, for example multibench env install --methods <method> --packed --run.

scan() shows the same per method in its env_ok column.

FileNotFoundError: ... 'conda' from mtb.run

No method environment is installed yet and this host has no conda. Install the method's environment with multibench env install --methods <method> --packed --run.

OSError naming envs_dir, with MULTIBENCH_RUN_MODE=prefix

Prefix mode is forced, but the environment is not under envs_dir.

Install it (multibench env install --methods <method> --packed --run), point MULTIBENCH_ENVS_DIR at the folder that holds it, or unset MULTIBENCH_RUN_MODE.

RuntimeError: no conda/mamba on this host; <env> has a packed archive - pass packed=True

Only a lockfile build needs conda. Pass packed=True (--packed on the command line).

ImportError: No module named scib from mtb.evaluate

multibench was installed with --no-deps or into another interpreter. Run pip install multibench-sc in the environment you import from.

cLISI / iLISI are NaN, with a warning naming knn_graph.o

Both need scib's compiled LISI helper, which ships as a Linux x86-64 binary. On other platforms evaluate() rebuilds it automatically when a C++ compiler (g++, c++ or clang++) is on PATH.

Without a compiler, install one (Xcode command-line tools on macOS) and rerun evaluate in a new Python session, or run the g++ command the warning prints. The other metrics are computed either way.

unsupported input format from mtb.io.to_canonical

Accepted inputs: .h5ad, .h5mu, .csv / .tsv, .loom, in-memory AnnData / MuData, or an already-canonical scMultiBench .h5. Convert other formats first.

For a whole dataset folder, use mtb.io.export_dataset or multibench convert.

Still broken? Open an issue with the output of python -c "import multibench as mtb; print(mtb.__version__)" and pip freeze.

Next: the Quickstart, or run a method with the Run a method tutorial.

docs.title: How scMultiBench works
docs.text: scMultiBench is a benchmark of single-cell multimodal omics integration methods, not a method itself. It evaluates them so you can pick one for your data; multibench is its Python API.

docs.title: What scMultiBench covers
docs.text:
Four scenarios, defined by how the input data are structured. They are the category values the API takes:

  • Vertical: several modalities measured in the same cells (e.g. CITE-seq, 10x Multiome).
  • Diagonal: modalities measured in different cells (e.g. scRNA-seq and scATAC-seq from separate experiments).
  • Mosaic: several batches, only some sharing a modality, joined by a paired batch.
  • Cross: several batches, each with every modality (e.g. one CITE-seq assay from several donors).
Details

Tasks. Dimension reduction, batch correction, clustering, classification, feature selection and imputation.

Data. Real and simulated datasets covering RNA, ADT and ATAC.

docs.title: How it evaluates
docs.text:
Each task has its own metric panel. The scores are combined into per-method rank scores.

Details

Metric panels.

  • Dimension reduction, batch correction, clustering: scIB metrics (kBET, iLISI, ASW, graph connectivity, PCR, ARI, NMI and others).
  • Classification: accuracy and F1.
  • Feature selection: marker overlap and correlation.
  • Imputation: RMSE.
  • Every task: runtime and peak memory.

In the package. mtb.evaluate computes the scIB metrics.

Rankings. The paper summarises them in a decision tree that recommends methods per scenario and task (Fig. 6). The interactive explorer shows the same rankings.

docs.title: Get going
docs.text:
• Install: pip install multibench-sc, then import multibench. See Installation.
  • First run: Quickstart.
  • Tutorials: vertical, diagonal, mosaic, cross, and the end-to-end walkthrough.
  • Explore: interactive Shiny explorer.
  • API: multibench.

docs.title: Quickstart
docs.text:
Five steps: find methods for your data, plot the stored results, run a method, score the run, and plot it next to the stored results. Only step 3 needs a method environment.

TL;DR

import multibench as mtb, pandas as pd

# 1. methods for unpaired RNA + ATAC (diagonal)
mtb.find_methods(category="diagonal", modalities=["rna", "atac"])

# 2. plot the stored diagonal table for dataset D28
df = mtb.load_results("diagonal", dataset="D28")
mtb.plot.bubble(df, metrics=["ARI", "NMI", "ASW"], save="fig.pdf")

# 3. run a method on D28 (needs the method's environment)
mtb.data.fetch("D28")
res = mtb.run("SCALEX", "diagonal",
              inputs=mtb.inputs_for("D28", "diagonal", "SCALEX"),
              out_dir="out/scalex_d28")

# 4. score it with scIB metrics
metrics = mtb.evaluate(res.output, labels=mtb.labels_for("D28", "diagonal", "SCALEX"), metrics="clustering")

# 5. plot it next to the stored table
mine = mtb.to_long(metrics, method="SCALEX_rerun", dataset="D28", category="diagonal")
mtb.plot.bubble(pd.concat([df, mine]), metrics=["ARI", "NMI", "ASW"])

docs.title: Step 1, Discover methods for your data
docs.text:
Pick the category that matches your data, then filter by the modalities you have:

  • vertical: several modalities measured in the same cells
  • diagonal: modalities measured in different cells
  • mosaic: several batches, only some sharing a modality
  • cross: several batches, each with every modality
import multibench as mtb

mtb.find_methods(category="diagonal", modalities=["rna", "atac"])
# -> ['SCALEX', 'Seurat_v5', 'scBridge', 'VIPCCA', 'Portal', 'uniPort', 'sciCAN', 'scJoint', 'GLUE',
#     'MultiMAP', 'iNMF', 'online_iNMF', 'Conos', 'Seurat_v3']

Inspect a candidate, or rank the candidates from the stored tables:

info = mtb.method_info("SCALEX")
info["env"], info["atac"], info["needs_labels"], info["reference"]["doi"]
# ('scmb_torch', 'gene_activity', False, '10.1038/s41467-022-33758-z')
info["runtime"]
# {'observed': [{'cells': 11014, 'dataset': 'D28', 'sec': 2233, 'source': 'manual'}], 'tier': 'slow', 'worst_sec': 2233, 'host': 'gpu', 'note': '...'}
mtb.recommend("diagonal", modalities=["rna", "atac"])
Details

More filters. find_methods also filters by task, needs_labels, atac, runnable and tunable; every filter must hold. See the reference.

Methods without stored scores. recommend lists them with grand_score NaN and names them in a warning.

Batch correction. recommend(..., metrics="batch") ranks on the batch-correction metrics instead.

docs.title: Step 2, Plot the stored results
docs.text:
The package ships the metric tables of the demo datasets. Load one as a tidy frame and draw the scIB-style bubble table.

df = mtb.load_results("diagonal", dataset="D28")          # 14 methods
fig = mtb.plot.bubble(df, metrics=["ARI", "NMI", "ASW"], save="fig.pdf")
Details

Published or re-run tables. source="published" (the default) loads the benchmark's scIB tables; source="rerun" loads the package's own runs, which the category tutorials use.

The two can hold different methods for one dataset (for D52: one published, eight re-run), so name the source when the method count matters. mtb.results_coverage(category) lists what each holds.

Other filters. load_results also takes methods, metrics and clustering (reference).

Several datasets. plot.bubble(..., aggregate="summary") ranks methods across datasets by averaging their per-dataset ranks.

docs.title: Step 3, Run a method
docs.text:
mtb.run runs one method in its own environment and loads its output; inputs_for returns a benchmark dataset's input files. Install the environment first: multibench env install --methods SCALEX --packed --run (Linux).

mtb.data.fetch("D28")                                      # 137 MB; no-op when present
res = mtb.run(
    method="SCALEX",
    category="diagonal",
    inputs=mtb.inputs_for("D28", "diagonal", "SCALEX"),    # {'rna': .../D28/rna.h5, 'atac_gas': .../D28/atac_gas.h5}
    out_dir="out/scalex_d28",
)

res.output      # the joint embedding
res.cmd         # the command that was executed
Details

Inputs. inputs maps each modality role to a file. Files that are not canonical scMultiBench .h5 are converted first; convert=False skips this. Relative paths are fine.

Environment. SCALEX runs in scmb_torch (mtb.method_info("SCALEX")["env"]). cmd_template="{cmd}" runs the command in the current environment instead.

The result. The RunResult also holds the method's captured stdout and stderr. A failed run raises RuntimeError with the end of that output.

From the shell. --dry-run prints the command without running it; drop it to run:

terminal
multibench run --method SCALEX --category diagonal \
    --input rna=<data_path>/D28/rna.h5 --input atac_gas=<data_path>/D28/atac_gas.h5 \
    --out-dir out/scalex_d28 --dry-run

docs.title: Your own data
docs.text:
Write your data as a dataset folder, check which methods fit it with scan, then run and score all of them with run_all.

print(mtb.describe_layout("vertical"))          # the files each category expects
mtb.io.export_dataset(adata, "data/MYCITE", rna="X", adt="obsm:protein", labels="obs:celltype")
mtb.scan("MYCITE", "vertical", data_path="data")     # files_ok / env_ok per method, with reasons
res = mtb.run_all("MYCITE", "vertical", data_path="data", out_dir="out/")
res.summary; res.plot()

docs.title: Step 4, Evaluate your run
docs.text:
mtb.evaluate scores an embedding with scIB metrics against the cell-type labels. Give labels_for the category and method, and pass its dict as it is: the files come back in the order that method stacks the cells.

metrics = mtb.evaluate(
    res.output,
    labels=mtb.labels_for("D28", "diagonal", "SCALEX"),   # {'rna_cty': ..., 'atac_cty': ...}
    metrics="clustering",
)
# index: ARI, NMI, ASW, iASW, iF1, cLISI   column: Value
Details

What is computed. metrics=None (the default) computes every applicable metric: the clustering family, plus the batch family when there is a batch vector or several label files. See the metrics= vocabulary.

Labels. labels can also be a pandas.Series, an array, or an obs column name when the output is an AnnData. A dict in another order needs label_order=.

Run time. ARI, NMI and iF1 need a Leiden resolution sweep, from seconds to minutes depending on the cell count. Pass your own clustering=, or a metrics= list without those three, to skip it.

docs.title: Step 5, Plot your own result
docs.text:
to_long turns the scores into the format load_results returns; plot it together with the stored table. Give your run a method name not already in the table: duplicate method names raise an error.

import pandas as pd

mine = mtb.to_long(metrics, method="SCALEX_rerun", dataset="D28", category="diagonal")

combined = pd.concat([df, mine], ignore_index=True)
mtb.plot.bubble(combined, metrics=["ARI", "NMI", "ASW"],
                title="D28: stored table + SCALEX re-run", save="compare.pdf")
Details

Re-runs. Methods are stochastic, so a re-run gives slightly different values from the stored table; compare ranks rather than decimals. See Are my numbers comparable?

A different dataset. When your rows come from another dataset than the stored ones, pass aggregate="summary" to rank within each dataset first.

docs.title: From the command line
docs.text:
Each step has a CLI equivalent; multibench <command> --help lists the flags.

terminal
multibench plot bubble --category diagonal --dataset D28 \
    --metrics ARI,NMI,ASW --out fig.pdf
# the CLI takes one label file: stack D28's two in the embedding's cell order
{ cat <data_path>/D28/rna_cty.csv; tail -n +2 <data_path>/D28/atac_cty.csv; } > d28_cty.csv
multibench evaluate --output out/scalex_d28/embedding.h5 --labels d28_cty.csv \
    --method SCALEX_rerun --dataset D28 --category diagonal --out mine.csv
multibench plot bubble --input mine.csv --category diagonal --dataset D28 \
    --metrics ARI,NMI,ASW --out compare.pdf
Details
  • list, find, params, scan, layout, convert, run, run-all, evaluate, plot, cite and env mirror the Python API.
  • scan prints a compact table; --columns all or --format csv|tsv|json gives every column.
  • run --dry-run and run-all --dry-run print the commands without running them.
  • --param METHOD:KEY=VALUE on run-all sets a hyperparameter; params METHOD lists them.
  • plot --input is repeatable; with --category it adds your rows to the stored table.
  • Tables go to stdout; progress and notes go to stderr.

docs.text:

  • Vertical / diagonal / mosaic / cross - one notebook per category: run_all on the reference dataset and on your own data.
  • Run a method - run any of the 36 methods with mtb.run.
  • Installation - the package and the method environments.
