docs.title: Diagonal integration¶
docs.text:
Diagonal integration combines RNA and ATAC measured in different cells, with no pairing between them. If your RNA and ATAC come from the same cells (10x multiome), use the vertical tutorial. Reference dataset: D28 (6,408 RNA + 4,606 ATAC cells).

Details

ATAC input. Most diagonal methods take ATAC as gene-activity scores, computed beforehand with a tool such as Signac or ArchR. A few take the peak matrix, alone or alongside the scores.

docs.title: 1. Install¶
docs.text:
pip install multibench-sc is all this notebook needs. Methods run in their own environments, downloaded only when you set INSTALL_ENVS = True (Linux or Colab).

Details

Default. With INSTALL_ENVS = False no environment is downloaded, only the reference data and stand-in outputs. Every cell runs; a method cell uses those outputs instead.

Running methods. Set INSTALL_ENVS = True on Colab or a Linux machine to download the prebuilt environments (no conda needed) and run the methods.

On Colab, choose a GPU runtime first (Runtime -> Change runtime type -> T4 GPU). On a CPU runtime the smaller CPU builds are installed and training methods are much slower.

docs.title: Environments - only if you will run methods¶
docs.text:
Installs the environments for online_iNMF, iNMF and scJoint (2 envs, 1.6 GB to download on a CPU host, 5.1 GB on a GPU host). The cell skips the download unless INSTALL_ENVS = True on Linux.

Details

Location. Environments are unpacked under mtb.config.DEFAULT.envs_dir (~/.cache/multibench/envs on a host without conda); set it before this cell to use another disk. Environments already there are skipped.

All diagonal methods. multibench env install --category diagonal --packed --run installs every diagonal environment (9 envs, 21.6 GB to download on a CPU host, 28.8 GB on a GPU host); multibench env plan --category diagonal lists the size of each.

docs.title: Run the methods¶
docs.text:
run_all runs online_iNMF, iNMF and scJoint on D28, each in its own environment, and scores each embedding with scIB metrics. Without environments, the cell prints one line and loads stand-in results.

Details

Stand-in. When none of these environments is installed, the cell downloads the benchmark host's run_all outputs for D28 with mtb.data.fetch_outputs (embeddings and run times included) and reloads them with mtb.load_batch.

Offline fallback. If that download fails, the cell uses the stored results (load_results(source="rerun")): status reads STORED, and there is no embedding to score.

docs.title: Score one embedding¶
docs.text:
run_all has already scored every method. To score one embedding yourself, pass the file the method wrote and the dataset's label files to mtb.evaluate:

Details

Label order. label_order= passes the order in which the method stacked its cells, taken from the run record's labels_used.

Choosing metrics. metrics= accepts:

  • None (the default): every applicable metric
  • "clustering", "batch" or "all": a family
  • a list such as ["ARI", "NMI"]: those metrics

Batch metrics need batch= or several label files.

docs.title: Plot¶
docs.text:
res.plot() draws a bubble table. Circle size is the method's rank in each column (largest = best); colour is the metric value, scaled within the column (darker = higher).

Details

Columns. Metrics are grouped by family: blue for dimension reduction and clustering, green for batch correction. Each family starts with an Overall bar; its length and colour both show the family score.

docs.title: 3. Your own data¶
docs.text: The same calls on a dataset folder the package has not seen. describe_layout prints the files a diagonal dataset needs and their format:

docs.title: 4. Stored results¶
docs.text:
The package ships stored results for 12 methods on D28 (source="rerun"). load_results reads them as a long table and mtb.plot.bubble draws it; nothing is run.

Details: sources

Two sources. For D28, the published table holds 14 methods and the package's own runs ("rerun") hold 12. load_results defaults to source="published", so every call here names its source. Where both hold a method, the values can differ.

Other datasets. Stored results also exist for D24 and D25 (mtb.available_datasets(CATEGORY, source="both")).

Your own runs. run_all saves its results in out_dir; mtb.load_batch(out_dir) reloads them later without running anything.

docs.title: What runs on a dataset, and why not¶
docs.text:
scan on D28, nothing run: the first table lists the variants whose data fits, with the install command for any missing environment (env_reason); the second, why the other variants do not fit.

Details

From the shell. multibench scan D28 --category diagonal prints the scan for every variant; --columns all adds every column, including command, the exact command run would execute.

docs.title: Tuning¶
docs.text:
The table counts the hyperparameters each variant exposes. mtb.params_for(method, CATEGORY, modalities) lists them; run_all(..., params={"Method": {"key": value}}) sets them.

Details

None exposed. Many upstream scripts set their hyperparameters in code; their variants accept no params.

From the shell. multibench params METHOD prints the table; multibench run-all ... --param METHOD:KEY=VALUE sets a value.

docs.title: A method's record and citation¶
docs.text:
method_info returns what the registry holds about a method, including its reference and repository; mtb.cite returns the citations for the benchmark and the methods you ran.

Details

needs_labels is True when any variant needs cell-type labels; each entry of supports gives it per variant.

verbose=True adds the long notes.

docs.title: The metrics¶
docs.text:
Two families; higher is better for every metric.

family metrics measures clustering / bio-conservation ARI, NMI, ASW, iASW, iF1, cLISI whether the embedding separates the annotated cell types batch correction ASW_batch, GC, iLISI (+ opt-in kBET) whether the batches mix within each cell type Details

Range. All lie in [0, 1] except ARI, which can be slightly negative.

Batch metrics appear only when the dataset has more than one batch.

kBET is computed only when named (metrics=["ASW_batch", "GC", "iLISI", "kBET"]); it is much slower than the others.

docs.title: Methods from the benchmark study¶
docs.text: The cell compares the methods the scMultiBench study benchmarked for diagonal integration with the methods this package has a diagonal variant for, and prints each missing method with the categories it has variants for.

docs.title: Troubleshooting¶
docs.text:
When a method is not runnable, scan's reason column says why; when a run fails, res.failures holds the error.

Details symptom fix files_ok False: input files not found the reason names the missing file and lists what the folder holds env_ok False run the multibench env install ... command in the reason ... which is cells x features the matrix is transposed: re-export with mtb.io.to_canonical or export_dataset a method fails res.failures.iloc[0]["error"] ends with the method's stderr a method times out raise timeout= in run_all low label_order_confidence several label files fit the cell count: check label_order_candidates in res.results batch metrics use the wrong batches res.rescore(batch=my_vector) re-scores without re-running

docs.title: Next steps¶
docs.text:
• the other tutorials: vertical, mosaic, cross
  • the interactive explorer: the full benchmark's rankings, no install needed
  • mtb.recommend(CATEGORY, modalities=[...]): a ranking of methods from the stored results
  • mtb.sweep(...): one method over a range of values of one hyperparameter

docs.title: Discover methods
docs.text:
These calls show which of the 36 registered methods fit your data and your task. They only read the package's registry: no environments, GPUs or data are needed.

TL;DR

import multibench as mtb

mtb.list_tasks()                                 # ['batch', 'classification', 'clustering', ...]
mtb.list_methods(category="vertical")            # every method in a category
mtb.find_methods(category="diagonal",            # filter by what your data has
                 modalities=["rna", "atac"],
                 needs_labels=False)
mtb.method_info("SCALEX")                        # everything known about one method
mtb.recommend("vertical", modalities=["rna", "adt"])   # ranked by stored scores
print(mtb.cite(["SCALEX"]))                      # the benchmark and the method, one line each

docs.title: The four integration categories
docs.text:
Pick the category that matches your experimental design and pass it as category= first. A method written for one design cannot take data from another.

Category Design Typical modalities vertical Several modalities measured in the same cells RNA+ADT, RNA+ATAC, RNA+ADT+ATAC diagonal Modalities measured in different cells, bridged by shared features RNA batch + ATAC batch mosaic Several batches, only some sharing a modality, joined by a paired batch mixed, partially paired cross Several batches, each with every modality replicate cohorts

docs.title: List what exists
docs.text:
list_tasks and list_methods show what the registry holds. list_methods filters by category only; to filter by task, use find_methods.

import multibench as mtb

mtb.list_tasks()
# ['batch', 'classification', 'clustering', 'dimension_reduction', 'imputation']

mtb.list_methods()                       # all 36 methods
mtb.list_methods(category="vertical")    # paired-design methods only
mtb.find_methods("diagonal", task="clustering")

docs.title: Filter by what your data has
docs.text:
find_methods filters by task and by what your data has: the modalities you measured, how your ATAC is encoded, and whether you have cell-type labels.

# unpaired RNA and ATAC batches, no cell-type labels
mtb.find_methods(category="diagonal", modalities=["rna", "atac"], needs_labels=False)
# ['SCALEX', 'Seurat_v5', 'VIPCCA', 'Portal', ...]

mtb.find_methods(category="diagonal", atac="gene_activity")   # ATAC as gene activity
mtb.find_methods(category="vertical", tunable=True)          # hyperparameters can be set
Details

How filters combine. A method matches when one of its variants meets all the filters together. None, the default, turns a filter off.

modalities. The variant must take every listed type, so ["rna"] is broad and ["rna", "atac"] stricter. protein means adt, and a role name such as atac_gas counts as atac.

atac. The ATAC representation the method's script reads: "gene_activity" (alias "gas") or "peak" (alias "peaks"). The role name can mislead: moETM, scMM and iPOLNG take a role called atac_gas but read peaks.

needs_labels. Judged per variant. method_info(m)["needs_labels"] is True when any variant needs labels: for scMoMaT only its mosaic variant does.

tunable. True keeps the methods whose command line exposes at least one hyperparameter for run(params=...).

Typos. An unknown token raises ValueError listing the valid values. A bare string such as modalities="rna" raises TypeError.

docs.title: Inspect a single method
docs.text:
method_info returns what the registry knows about one method: its variants, environment, label needs, observed runtime and reference.

info = mtb.method_info("SCALEX")
info["env"], info["atac"], info["needs_labels"]   # ('scmb_torch', 'gene_activity', False)
info["supports"]     # one entry per variant: category, modalities, output kind, labels
info["runtime"]      # {'observed': [...], 'tier': 'slow', 'worst_sec': 2233, ...}
print(mtb.cite("SCALEX"))                         # the benchmark and the method, one line each
Details

Runtime. observed lists measured runs (dataset, cells, seconds) and tier summarises them, from fast to very_slow. Use it to set run_all(timeout=...). On a CPU, training methods take much longer than these times.

Hyperparameters. mtb.params_for(method) lists what run(params=...) can change and what the script fixes.

Catalog columns. deep_learning and output are in mtb.catalog.methods(), not in method_info.

Citing. mtb.cite("SCALEX", "GLUE") takes one id per argument or one list. fmt="bibtex" returns .bib entries.

Unknown ids raise KeyError with a did-you-mean hint.

docs.title: Rank from stored results
docs.text:
recommend ranks a category's methods by their stored scores and shows how many datasets each was scored on (coverage).

mtb.recommend("vertical", modalities=["rna", "adt"])
#   method  grand_score  n_datasets  n_datasets_total  coverage  needs_labels  runtime_tier  worst_sec ...
Details

Unscored methods. Methods that fit the category but have no stored scores are listed last, with grand_score NaN and coverage 0.0. One UserWarning names them, and any datasets left out for having too few methods.

Other sources. source="rerun" ranks the package's re-run tables instead of the published ones. To rank your own method alongside, pass long_df=pd.concat([mtb.load_results(category), mine]).

Metrics. metrics= picks the metric family; the default ranks on the clustering metrics.

needs_labels here follows the category's variants: scMoMaT is False in a vertical ranking.

docs.title: The full benchmark catalog
docs.text:
mtb.catalog returns the benchmark's method, dataset and metric tables as DataFrames, and maps free-text names to canonical ones.

from multibench import catalog

catalog.methods()                    # one row per method: language, deep_learning, atac, output, ...
catalog.datasets()                   # one row per dataset: simulated, category, has_results, ...
catalog.metrics()                    # the metric details
catalog.canonical_id("Seurat v5")    # 'Seurat_v5'
catalog.canonical_metric("kbet")     # 'kBET'
Details

Datasets. catalog.datasets() also lists the ids that exist only as stored results, such as the re-run subsamples D11s and D28s. The simulated column marks the simulated datasets.

Unknown names. canonical_id returns an unknown name unchanged; canonical_id(name, strict=True) raises KeyError instead.

Metric codes. catalog.known_metrics() lists the ten scIB codes and PCR.

docs.title: Before running
docs.text:
Check your folder with mtb.scan("MYDATA", category): it reports files_ok and env_ok per method. Then run them with run_all.

Next: run a chosen method in Run a method, score it in Evaluate a run, and compare methods in Load and plot results.

import h5py

def stand_in(dataset, method):
    """`method`'s embedding from the benchmark host's run_all outputs; None if that download fails."""
    try:
        batch = mtb.load_batch(mtb.data.fetch_outputs(dataset), methods=[method])
        with h5py.File(Path(batch.out_dir) / f"{method}_{dataset}" / "embedding.h5") as f:
            emb = f["data"][()]
        print(f"stand-in: {method}'s embedding from the benchmark host's run_all outputs for {dataset} (fetch_outputs)")
        return emb
    except Exception as e:                                   # offline, or the outputs are not published yet
        print(f"stand-in: the package's stored scores for {method} ({type(e).__name__} from fetch_outputs: {e})")
        return None

check = mtb.scan(DATASET, CATEGORY, methods=["Matilda"])

    emb = res.output

def stored_table(kind, dataset):
    """The `summary` or `long_all` table for `dataset`: from results/, else from the package's stored results."""
    if RESULTS.is_dir():
        return pd.read_csv(RESULTS / f"{kind}_{dataset}.csv")
    long = mtb.load_results(dataset=dataset, source="rerun")
    if kind == "long_all":
        return long
    return long.pivot_table(index="method", columns="metric", values="value").rename_axis(columns=None).reset_index()

docs.title: Multi-Task Omics — multibench end-to-end tutorial¶
docs.text:
This notebook takes one dataset, D11 (CITE-seq PBMC, 2,864 cells, RNA + ADT), through the whole workflow: find a method, resolve its inputs, check its parameters, run it, score it and plot the scores.

inputs_for  →  params_for  →  run  →  evaluate  →  plot
 (data)        (tuning)      (method)  (metrics)   (figure)

docs.title: 0. Setup¶
docs.text:
The first cell installs multibench-sc if it is missing. Methods run in their own environments, downloaded only when you set INSTALL_ENVS = True (Linux or Colab).

Details

Default. With INSTALL_ENVS = False no environment is downloaded. Every cell runs; section 4 loads a stand-in for the Matilda run.

Running methods. Set INSTALL_ENVS = True on Colab or a Linux machine to download Matilda's prebuilt environment (no conda needed) and run it.

On Colab, choose a GPU runtime first (Runtime -> Change runtime type -> T4 GPU). On a CPU runtime the smaller CPU build is installed and training is much slower.

Stored tables. Sections 7 and 8 read results/ when the notebook runs from the repository's notebooks/ folder. Elsewhere, as on Colab, they read the package's stored results, which have no status or run-time columns.

docs.title: Environments¶
docs.text:
Methods run in dedicated environments; the next cell lists the one each method uses. Section 4 runs Matilda: the cell after it installs Matilda's environment when INSTALL_ENVS = True on Linux.

Details

From a terminal. multibench env install --methods Matilda --packed --run installs the same environment. Give --methods a comma-separated list, or use --category vertical for every vertical method.

--packed downloads a prebuilt archive, so no conda is needed. Without it the environment is built with conda from its lockfile.

Dry run. Without --run, env install only prints what it would install; multibench env doctor --methods Matilda shows whether it is installed.

Location. Environments are unpacked under mtb.config.DEFAULT.envs_dir; set it before the install cell to use another disk.

docs.title: 1. Discovery — which methods fit my data?¶
docs.text: find_methods lists the methods that support a category; method_info describes one method.

docs.title: 2. Data — resolve the inputs¶
docs.text: mtb.data.fetch downloads D11 once. inputs_for returns the files a method needs from a dataset; check=True raises an error now if one is missing.

docs.title: 3. Parameters — what can I tune?¶
docs.text:
params_for lists a method's parameters: defaults are passed on every run, tunable are the options the method's script accepts. Change any of them with run(..., params={...}).

Details

Empty tunable. 9 of these 14 methods expose no parameters on their command line, so they cannot be tuned through the package. The second table shows which.

Upstream defaults. The values under tunable are the script's own defaults; p["effective"] holds the value a run uses. The params_for reference lists the other keys.

docs.title: 4. Run a method¶
docs.text:
run runs Matilda in its environment and loads the embedding it writes. params={"epochs": 5} shortens training for this demo. Without the environment, the cell prints one line and loads a stand-in.

Details

Stand-in. The cell downloads the benchmark host's run_all outputs for D11 with mtb.data.fetch_outputs, reloads them with mtb.load_batch and reads Matilda's embedding from them.

Offline fallback. If that download fails, emb is None and section 5 shows Matilda's stored scores (load_results(source="rerun")) instead of computing them.

docs.title: Not every method returns an embedding¶
docs.text:
Check a method's output kind before computing metrics: 12 of these methods return an embedding, 2 return a graph. Scoring a graph as an embedding gives a meaningless result and no error.

Details

The two graph methods.

  • Seurat_WNN writes only a neighbour graph, so there is nothing to score.
  • scMoMaT writes a KNN graph plus a UMAP embedding, which run returns in res.extra.

With run_all. mtb.run_all checks the kind for you. It scores scMoMaT through its UMAP (status CHAIN_OK_GRAPH_METHOD) and reports Seurat_WNN as RUN_OK_NO_EMBEDDING.

docs.title: 5. Evaluate — scIB metrics¶
docs.text:
evaluate scores the embedding against the cell-type labels. Pass the labels in the embedding's cell order.

Details

Metrics. metrics="clustering" computes ARI, NMI, ASW, iASW, iF1 and cLISI.

Batch metrics. D11 has a single batch, so batch metrics do not apply.

docs.title: 6. Plot¶
docs.text: to_long reshapes the scores into a long table; plot.bubble draws it.

docs.title: 7. Comparing all 14 methods¶
docs.text: Running all 14 methods takes hours, so this section loads their stored D11 results. Seurat_WNN has no scores: it returns a graph, not an embedding.

docs.title: 8. The other integration categories¶
docs.text:
Each category has its own reference dataset. Repeat the calls above with its dataset, category and a modality list the method accepts (mtb.method_info(m)["supports"]). For a dataset with several label files, pass labels_for(dataset, category, method) to evaluate (see Label order below).

category data reference dataset vertical several modalities measured in the same cells D11 (2,864 cells) diagonal RNA and ATAC measured in different cells D28 (11,014 cells) mosaic several batches; only some share a modality D45 (32,151 cells) cross several batches, each with all modalities D52 (23,478 cells) Details: method counts

Counts. The next cell counts the methods with a variant for the dataset's files (scan, files_ok); find_methods alone checks only the modality types. A dataset must be on disk to be counted.

docs.title: Stored results for each category¶
docs.text:
Details

Conos on D28. Its ARI is near 0. load_results(source="rerun") flags this row with DegenerateRerunWarning; leave it out when ranking.

docs.title: Label order¶
docs.text:
A method that stacks several batches or modalities sets its own cell order. labels_for(dataset, category, method) returns the label files in that order, and evaluate takes the dict as is. A wrong order gives a wrong score and no error.

mtb.evaluate(emb, labels=mtb.labels_for("D52", "cross", "StabMap"))   # cty3, cty1, cty2
Details

In the stored results. The label_order column of each stored summary shows the order used. StabMap on D52 puts batch 3 first (cty3+cty1+cty2) and uniPort on D28 puts ATAC before RNA; labels_for with the method returns both orders.

Concerto. Its stored D52 run put batch 3 first: Concerto stacks its batches in the order the filesystem lists its per-batch files. mtb.run has them listed in batch order, so labels_for("D52", "cross", "Concerto") returns cty1, cty2, cty3, the order of a new run. Score the stored run with label_order= set to its label_order column.

Your own dict. A dict you build or reorder yourself goes in as is only in the default order (cty1, cty2, ...; RNA before ATAC); name any other order with label_order=.

Fewer batches. A method that uses only some label files takes only those keys: UINMF on D52 uses label_order=["cty1", "cty2"].

With run_all. mtb.run_all tries every label order that matches the cell count, keeps the one with the highest ARI and reports it in the summary columns label_order and label_order_confidence.

docs.title: Reading the bubble chart¶
docs.text:
In plot.bubble, size is a rank and colour a scaled value, both relative to the methods plotted, so small score gaps can look large. Read the values in the table below the figure.

Details

Example. On D52, sciPENN (0.6947), UINMF (0.6905) and StabMap (0.6880) differ by less than 0.007 ARI but get different bubble sizes.

docs.title: Run time¶
docs.text:
Some methods take hours even on small datasets. Check mtb.method_info(m)["runtime"] before running a method.

Details

Examples.

method dataset (cells) run time sciPENN D11 (2,864) 143 s scJoint D28 (11,014) 209 s scMSI D11 (2,864) 2.3 h MultiVI D45 (32,151) 3.3 h sciCAN D28 (11,014) 4.4 h

Without a GPU, training methods take much longer than these times.

Time limits. A run_all(timeout=...) run that exceeds the limit ends with status TIMEOUT; allow hours for the slow methods.

docs.title: Evaluate a run
docs.text:
mtb.evaluate scores a run output (an embedding) against cell-type labels and returns the scIB metrics.

TL;DR

import multibench as mtb

metrics = mtb.evaluate(
    result.output,                        # the embedding from mtb.run
    labels=mtb.labels_for("D11")["cty"],  # one label per cell, in row order
    metrics="clustering",
)
print(metrics)

docs.title: Choose the metrics
docs.text:
metrics= takes a family ("clustering", "batch", "all") or a list of metric codes. The default computes every metric your inputs allow.

labels = mtb.labels_for("D11")["cty"]

mtb.evaluate(result.output, labels=labels, metrics=["ASW"])
mtb.evaluate(result.output, labels=labels, clustering=my_clusters,   # your own clusters
             metrics=["ARI", "NMI"])
Details

Leiden sweep. ARI, NMI and iF1 need scIB's Leiden resolution sweep on the embedding. A list without these three skips it.

Your own clusters. clustering= replaces the sweep for ARI and NMI. iF1 still runs it unless you leave iF1 out.

kBET is computed only when a list names it, and can take hours on large datasets.

docs.title: Inputs
docs.text:
Pass the embedding and one cell-type label per cell, in the embedding's row order. Both can be paths or in-memory objects; the reference lists the accepted forms.

Details

Cell ids. A Series indexed by cell id is aligned by id when the output is indexed by cell id too: an AnnData or .h5ad, or a DataFrame indexed by cell id. Otherwise it is matched by position, with a warning. Plain arrays, lists and label files are always matched by position.

docs.title: Batch metrics
docs.text:
Batch metrics also need one batch per cell: pass batch=, or the mtb.labels_for dict of a multi-batch dataset, whose files then serve as batches. Give labels_for the category and method, so the files come in the order the method stacked its cells.

mtb.evaluate(
    result.output,                                      # a StabMap run on D52
    labels=mtb.labels_for("D52", "cross", "StabMap"),   # cty3, cty1, cty2: each file is a batch
    metrics="all",
)
Details

File order. Without a method, labels_for uses the default order: numbered files ascending, rna before adt before atac. StabMap stacks its reference batch first, cty3 on D52; a wrong order gives wrong scores without an error. run_all detects each method's order and records it in summary.label_order.

Your own dict. A dict you build or reorder yourself goes in as is only in the default order; name any other order with label_order=.

Batches inside one file. run_all also uses each cell's label file as its batch, so batches inside one file (donors, say) are not scored. Re-score the saved outputs with the real vector; nothing is re-run:

res = mtb.load_batch("out/")
rescored = res.rescore(batch=my_batch_vector)

docs.title: The result
docs.text:
A DataFrame indexed by metric name with one Value column, the shape of the benchmark's metric.csv. A metric that cannot run on your machine is NaN, with a warning; the others are still computed.

metrics.to_csv("metric.csv")
Details

cLISI and iLISI need scib's compiled LISI helper. Where the binary scib ships cannot run, evaluate rebuilds it once if a C++ compiler (g++, c++ or clang++) is on PATH. Otherwise the warning prints the build command.

kBET needs R through rpy2; without it kBET is NaN.

docs.title: Are my numbers comparable?
docs.text:
To compare with the stored tables, score against the dataset's own labels (mtb.labels_for) with the default clustering. Most methods are stochastic: compare ranks, not decimals.

Details

Default clustering. scIB's optimal-resolution Leiden sweep: ten resolutions from 0.2 to 2.0, keeping the one with the highest NMI against the labels.

Leiden backend. The sweep runs on igraph by default. mtb.config.DEFAULT.leiden_flavor = "leidenalg" switches to the backend scib itself uses; scores can differ slightly between the two.

Isolated-label metrics. iASW and iF1 score every cell type, whereas scib's default scores only types confined to few batches.

docs.title: Reshape for plotting
docs.text:
mtb.to_long turns the result into the long frame mtb.load_results returns, so it can be concatenated with a stored table. Its source column reads user.

mine = mtb.to_long(metrics, method="MyMethod", dataset="D11", category="vertical")

Next: draw it next to the stored tables in Load and plot results.

def stored_sweep(dataset, methods=None):
    """The stored results for `dataset`, as the object `run_all` returns."""
    long = mtb.load_results(CATEGORY, dataset=dataset, source="rerun", methods=methods)
    recs = [{"method": m, "status": "STORED", "metrics": g.set_index("metric")["value"].to_dict()}
            for m, g in long.groupby("method")]
    return mtb.BatchResult(recs, dataset, CATEGORY)

def stand_in(dataset, methods, stored):
    """The benchmark host's run_all outputs for `dataset`; the stored results if that download fails."""
    try:
        res = mtb.load_batch(mtb.data.fetch_outputs(dataset), methods=methods)
        print(f"stand-in: the benchmark host's run_all outputs for {dataset} (fetch_outputs) - real embeddings and run times")
        return res
    except Exception as e:                                   # offline, or the outputs are not published yet
        print(f"stand-in: the package's stored metric table ({type(e).__name__} from fetch_outputs: {e})")
        return stored_sweep(*stored)

Put your files in  <data_path>/<DATASET_NAME>/ , e.g. ./data/MYDATA/
  (dataset = the folder name; data_path = the folder that contains it)

LAYOUT FOR MOSAIC:
  rna1.h5 rna2.h5 atac2.h5 atac3.h5   <- numbered, one per batch
  cty1.csv cty2.csv cty3.csv          <- one per batch

  (numbered files live in the same flat dir; there is no batch column)

Modality roles and the filenames they resolve to:
    rna              rna.h5      - gene expression
    adt              adt.h5      - surface protein (CITE-seq antibody-derived tags)
    atac             atac.h5     - chromatin accessibility
    atac_gas         atac.h5     - ATAC as gene-activity scores  <-- note: plain atac.h5
    atac_peak        peak.h5     - ATAC as peaks                 <-- note: peak.h5, not atac.h5
    rna1/rna2/...    rna1.h5, rna2.h5, ... - one file per batch (mosaic/cross)
    adt1/adt2/...    adt1.h5, adt2.h5, ... - one file per batch (mosaic/cross)
    cty              cty.csv     - cell-type labels, one label set (vertical)
    rna_cty / atac_cty rna_cty.csv, atac_cty.csv - one label file per modality, used when RNA and ATAC come from different cells (diagonal)
    cty1/cty2/...    cty1.csv, cty2.csv, ... - one label file per batch (mosaic/cross)

!! ATAC: the role name does not guarantee the representation.
   atac_gas resolves to atac_gas.h5 if present, otherwise FALLS BACK
   to atac.h5 - and a multiome atac.h5 usually holds peaks, not gene
   activity. Check the feature names: chr1:3094772-3095489 is a peak,
   a gene symbol is gene activity.
   atac_peak resolves to atac_peak.h5, else peak.h5.
   This matters because methods disagree (lists from the registry;
   see mtb.find_methods(atac=...) / mtb.method_info(m)['atac']):
     need GENE ACTIVITY: SCALEX/scBridge/scMDC/Matilda/VIPCCA/Portal/uniPort/sciCAN/scJoint/UnitedNet/iNMF/online_iNMF/Conos
     need PEAKS:         Multigrate/Seurat_v5/MultiVI/Cobolt/scMVP/scMM/scMoMaT/moETM/MIRA/VIMCCA/SMILE/GLUE/MultiMAP/iPOLNG/StabMap/Seurat_v3/Seurat_WNN
   Feeding the wrong one runs to completion and returns a plausible
   but WRONG embedding - no error.
   Check what you actually have before trusting a cross-dataset result.
   scan() flags the commonest trap in its `caveat` column: an atac_gas
   role that fell back to an atac.h5 whose features are chr:start-end.

MODALITY FILE FORMAT (.h5) - easiest route first:
  mtb.io.to_canonical(src, dst)   converts an .h5ad and writes
  everything below correctly. Prefer it over building the file by hand.
  For a whole dataset in one call (every modality + labels, numbered
  per batch when batch= is given):
    mtb.io.export_dataset(adata, '<data_path>/MYDATA', rna='X',
                          adt='obsm:protein', labels='obs:cell_type')
  Both store matrix/data as float64, gzip-compressed and chunked, like
  the shipped files (a 3000x2000 8%-dense matrix is ~1.5 MB on disk).

  If you do build it yourself, all three datasets are required:
    matrix/data      the matrix, stored FEATURES x CELLS
    matrix/features  one entry per feature (row of matrix/data)
    matrix/barcodes  one entry per cell    (column of matrix/data)
  e.g. 2,000 genes x 5,000 cells -> matrix/data has shape (2000, 5000),
  matrix/features has 2000 entries and matrix/barcodes has 5000.
  Note: this is the TRANSPOSE of the scanpy/AnnData convention
  (AnnData.X is cells x genes). scan() rejects a transposed file, and
  a file with only matrix/data fails with a KeyError about 'features'.
Labels are a single-column CSV: one header line (typically 'x'),
then one cell-type label per cell; the evaluator reads the first
column and skips the header.

mosaic: Several batches where only some share a modality; a paired batch bridges the others.


ENVIRONMENTS
  Every method runs in its own conda env (they need mutually
  incompatible framework versions). scan() checks two gates per row -
  files_ok (the inputs are on disk, oriented and labelled) and env_ok
  (that conda env exists) - and marks a method runnable only when both
  pass, so a sweep never starts one that cannot finish.
      multibench env doctor          # what is needed / what is missing
      multibench env install --run   # build them all from lockfiles
      multibench env install --methods X --packed --run   # just one

Then:  mtb.scan('MYDATA')  ->  mtb.run_all('MYDATA', '<category>', out_dir=...)

labels_for returns a dataset's label files: cty1, cty2, ... in that order. Some methods stack their cells in another order; labels_for(DATASET, CATEGORY, method) returns the files in that method's order. A wrong order gives wrong scores without an error.

Details: label order

On D45, labels_for returns another order for MultiVI (cty1, cty3, cty2) and SMILE (cty2, cty1, cty3).

With evaluate. Pass the dict labels_for returns as is. A dict you build or reorder yourself goes in as is only in the default order; name any other order with label_order=.

Check. run_all scores every order that fits the cell count and keeps the one with the highest ARI; the label_order column of res.summary shows it.

A real dataset under a new name: a random 60% of D46's cells, capped at 2,000 cells and 5,000 features per file.

Details: cell alignment

Alignment. Files with the same number of cells keep the same cells in the same order, so each modality file stays aligned with its label file. An export of your own data must keep this alignment.

In [11]: Copied! 
import os
import h5py
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

def subsample_dataset(src_dir, dst_dir, frac=0.6, seed=0, max_cells=2000, max_features=5000):
    """Copy a dataset under a new name, keeping a random `frac` of its cells; files with the same cell count keep the same cells."""
    rng = np.random.default_rng(seed)
    os.makedirs(dst_dir, exist_ok=True)
    counts, keep = {}, {}
    for fn in sorted(os.listdir(src_dir)):
        p = os.path.join(src_dir, fn)
        if fn.endswith(".h5"):
            with h5py.File(p) as f:
                if "matrix/data" in f:
                    counts[fn] = f["matrix/data"].shape[1]   # features x cells
        elif fn.endswith(".csv"):
            counts[fn] = len(pd.read_csv(p))
    for n in set(counts.values()):
        k = min(max(50, int(n * frac)), max_cells)
        keep[n] = np.sort(rng.choice(n, size=k, replace=False))
    for fn, n in counts.items():
        sp, dp = os.path.join(src_dir, fn), os.path.join(dst_dir, fn)
        idx = keep[n]
        if fn.endswith(".csv"):
            pd.read_csv(sp).iloc[idx].to_csv(dp, index=False)
        else:
            with h5py.File(sp) as f, h5py.File(dp, "w") as g:
                grp = g.create_group("matrix")
                n_feat = f["matrix/data"].shape[0]
                fidx = np.arange(n_feat) if n_feat <= max_features else np.sort(rng.choice(n_feat, size=max_features, replace=False))
                block = f["matrix/data"][fidx, :] if n_feat > max_features else f["matrix/data"][()]
                grp.create_dataset("data", data=np.asarray(block)[:, idx])
                if "matrix/features" in f:
                    grp.create_dataset("features", data=np.asarray(f["matrix/features"])[fidx])
                if "matrix/barcodes" in f:
                    grp.create_dataset("barcodes", data=np.asarray(f["matrix/barcodes"])[idx])
    return dst_dir

paper = ['MultiVI', 'scMoMaT', 'StabMap', 'Cobolt', 'UINMF', 'Multigrate', 'SMILE', 'scMM', 'moETM', 'UnitedNet', 'totalVI', 'sciPENN']   # benchmarked for mosaic on the tasks this package covers
registry = set(mtb.list_methods())
wired = sorted(m for m in registry
               if any(v["category"] == CATEGORY for v in mtb.method_info(m)["supports"]))
missing = [m for m in paper if m not in wired]
print(f"the study benchmarks {len(paper)} methods for {CATEGORY} on the tasks this package covers; this package has a variant for {len(wired)}")
for m in missing:
    if m in registry:
        info = mtb.method_info(m)
        print(f"  {m}: variants for {', '.join(info['categories'])} only (tasks: {', '.join(info['tasks'])})")
    else:
        print(f"  {m}: not in the registry")
if not missing:
    print("every benchmarked method has a variant for this category")
paper = ['MultiVI', 'scMoMaT', 'StabMap', 'Cobolt', 'UINMF', 'Multigrate', 'SMILE', 'scMM', 'moETM', 'UnitedNet', 'totalVI', 'sciPENN'] # benchmarked for mosaic on the tasks this package covers registry = set(mtb.list_methods()) wired = sorted(m for m in registry if any(v["category"] == CATEGORY for v in mtb.method_info(m)["supports"])) missing = [m for m in paper if m not in wired] print(f"the study benchmarks {len(paper)} methods for {CATEGORY} on the tasks this package covers; this package has a variant for {len(wired)}") for m in missing: if m in registry: info = mtb.method_info(m) print(f" {m}: variants for {', '.join(info['categories'])} only (tasks: {', '.join(info['tasks'])})") else: print(f" {m}: not in the registry") if not missing: print("every benchmarked method has a variant for this category") 
the study benchmarks 12 methods for mosaic on the tasks this package covers; this package has a variant for 6
  UINMF: variants for vertical, cross only (tasks: batch, clustering)
  scMM: variants for vertical, cross only (tasks: batch, clustering)
  moETM: variants for vertical only (tasks: clustering)
  UnitedNet: variants for vertical only (tasks: clustering, classification)
  totalVI: variants for vertical, cross only (tasks: batch, clustering)
  sciPENN: variants for vertical, cross only (tasks: batch, clustering, dimension_reduction, imputation)

docs.title: Mosaic integration¶
docs.text: Mosaic integration combines batches that share only some modalities, for example an RNA-only batch, an ATAC-only batch and a paired batch that links them. Which methods apply depends on the batch pattern; scan reports it. Reference dataset: D45 (32,151 cells).

docs.title: 1. Install¶
docs.text:
pip install multibench-sc is all this notebook needs. Methods run in their own environments, downloaded only when you set INSTALL_ENVS = True (Linux or Colab).

Details

Default. With INSTALL_ENVS = False no environment is downloaded, only the reference data and stand-in outputs. Every cell runs; a method cell uses those outputs instead.

Running methods. Set INSTALL_ENVS = True on Colab or a Linux machine to download the prebuilt environments (no conda needed) and run the methods.

On Colab, choose a GPU runtime first (Runtime -> Change runtime type -> T4 GPU). On a CPU runtime the smaller CPU builds are installed and training methods are much slower.

docs.title: Environments - only if you will run methods¶
docs.text:
Installs the environments for StabMap and scMoMaT (2 envs, 1.8 GB to download on a CPU host, 5.5 GB on a GPU host). The cell skips the download unless INSTALL_ENVS = True on Linux.

Details

Location. Environments are unpacked under mtb.config.DEFAULT.envs_dir (~/.cache/multibench/envs on a host without conda); set it before this cell to use another disk. Environments already there are skipped.

All mosaic methods. multibench env install --category mosaic --packed --run installs every mosaic environment (6 envs, 15.6 GB to download on a CPU host, 20.8 GB on a GPU host); multibench env plan --category mosaic lists the size of each.

docs.title: Run the methods¶
docs.text:
run_all runs StabMap and scMoMaT on D46, each in its own environment, and scores each embedding with scIB metrics. Without environments, the cell prints one line and loads stand-in results.

Details

Stand-in. When none of these environments is installed, the cell downloads the benchmark host's run_all outputs for D46 with mtb.data.fetch_outputs (embeddings and run times included) and reloads them with mtb.load_batch.

Offline fallback. If that download fails, the cell uses the stored results (load_results(source="rerun")): status reads STORED, and there is no embedding to score.

Dataset. These methods run on D46, whose batch pattern they accept. The stored-results fallback shows the D45 results instead.

docs.title: Score one embedding¶
docs.text:
run_all has already scored every method. To score one embedding yourself, pass the file the method wrote and the dataset's label files to mtb.evaluate:

Details

Label order. label_order= passes the order in which the method stacked its cells, taken from the run record's labels_used.

Choosing metrics. metrics= accepts:

  • None (the default): every applicable metric
  • "clustering", "batch" or "all": a family
  • a list such as ["ARI", "NMI"]: those metrics

Batch metrics need batch= or several label files.

docs.title: Plot¶
docs.text:
res.plot() draws a bubble table. Circle size is the method's rank in each column (largest = best); colour is the metric value, scaled within the column (darker = higher).

Details

Columns. Metrics are grouped by family: blue for dimension reduction and clustering, green for batch correction. Each family starts with an Overall bar; its length and colour both show the family score.

docs.title: 3. Your own data¶
docs.text: The same calls on a dataset folder the package has not seen. describe_layout prints the files a mosaic dataset needs and their format:

docs.title: 4. Stored results¶
docs.text:
The package ships stored results for 4 methods on D45 (source="rerun"). load_results reads them as a long table and mtb.plot.bubble draws it; nothing is run.

Details: sources

One source. There are no scIB tables for mosaic under source="published", the default, which raises FileNotFoundError; source="rerun" is the only stored source.

Your own runs. run_all saves its results in out_dir; mtb.load_batch(out_dir) reloads them later without running anything.

docs.title: What runs on a dataset, and why not¶
docs.text:
scan on D45, nothing run: the first table lists the variants whose data fits, with the install command for any missing environment (env_reason); the second, why the other variants do not fit.

Details

From the shell. multibench scan D45 --category mosaic prints the scan for every variant; --columns all adds every column, including command, the exact command run would execute.

docs.title: Tuning¶
docs.text:
The table counts the hyperparameters each variant exposes. mtb.params_for(method, CATEGORY, modalities) lists them; run_all(..., params={"Method": {"key": value}}) sets them.

Details

None exposed. Many upstream scripts set their hyperparameters in code; their variants accept no params.

From the shell. multibench params METHOD prints the table; multibench run-all ... --param METHOD:KEY=VALUE sets a value.

docs.title: A method's record and citation¶
docs.text:
method_info returns what the registry holds about a method, including its reference and repository; mtb.cite returns the citations for the benchmark and the methods you ran.

Details

needs_labels is True when any variant needs cell-type labels; each entry of supports gives it per variant.

verbose=True adds the long notes.

docs.title: The metrics¶
docs.text:
Two families; higher is better for every metric.

family metrics measures clustering / bio-conservation ARI, NMI, ASW, iASW, iF1, cLISI whether the embedding separates the annotated cell types batch correction ASW_batch, GC, iLISI (+ opt-in kBET) whether the batches mix within each cell type Details

Range. All lie in [0, 1] except ARI, which can be slightly negative.

Batch metrics appear only when the dataset has more than one batch.

kBET is computed only when named (metrics=["ASW_batch", "GC", "iLISI", "kBET"]); it is much slower than the others.

docs.title: Methods from the benchmark study¶
docs.text:
The cell compares the methods the scMultiBench study benchmarked for mosaic integration with the methods this package has a mosaic variant for, and prints each missing method with the categories it has variants for.

Details

UINMF has no mosaic variant: its script takes the second batch's unshared features from the first batch, which fails when the two are different modalities, and it accepts exactly two batches, a pattern that fits no mosaic dataset here.

docs.title: Troubleshooting¶
docs.text:
When a method is not runnable, scan's reason column says why; when a run fails, res.failures holds the error.

Details symptom fix files_ok False: input files not found the reason names the missing file and lists what the folder holds env_ok False run the multibench env install ... command in the reason ... which is cells x features the matrix is transposed: re-export with mtb.io.to_canonical or export_dataset a method fails res.failures.iloc[0]["error"] ends with the method's stderr a method times out raise timeout= in run_all low label_order_confidence several label files fit the cell count: check label_order_candidates in res.results batch metrics use the wrong batches res.rescore(batch=my_vector) re-scores without re-running

docs.title: Next steps¶
docs.text:
• the other tutorials: vertical, diagonal, cross
  • the interactive explorer: the full benchmark's rankings, no install needed
  • mtb.recommend(CATEGORY, modalities=[...]): a ranking of methods from the stored results
  • mtb.sweep(...): one method over a range of values of one hyperparameter

docs.title: Load and plot results
docs.text:
mtb.load_results reads the stored metric tables into one long frame; mtb.plot.bubble draws the scIB-style bubble table from it.

TL;DR

import multibench as mtb

df = mtb.load_results("vertical", dataset="D11")
fig = mtb.plot.bubble(df, metrics=["ARI", "NMI", "ASW", "cLISI"],
                      title="Vertical integration, D11", save="d11.pdf")

The same panel from the shell:

terminal
multibench plot bubble --category vertical --dataset D11 \
    --metrics ARI,NMI,ASW,cLISI --out d11.pdf

docs.title: Step 1, Load a tidy results frame
docs.text:
load_results returns one row per method, dataset and metric. Every plotting function takes this frame.

import multibench as mtb

df = mtb.load_results(
    "vertical",            # vertical | diagonal | mosaic | cross
    dataset="D11",         # a list for several; omit for all
    source="published",    # published | rerun | both
)
df.head()
#   metric     value      method dataset  category clustering     source
# 0    NMI  0.792936  Multigrate     D11  vertical    default  published
# 1    ARI  0.759446  Multigrate     D11  vertical    default  published
# 2    ASW  0.656011  Multigrate     D11  vertical    default  published
# ...
Details

Filters. methods= and metrics= narrow the frame and accept aliases ("mofa+" for MOFA2). metrics= takes the same values as in evaluate.

Your own tables. result_path= reads a long CSV you saved, or another results root, instead of the shipped tables.

docs.title: Published and re-run tables
docs.text:
source= picks the table: "published" (the default, the scIB tables), "rerun" (the package's own re-run sweeps) or "both". mtb.available_datasets(category, source=...) lists the datasets each holds.

Details

Datasets per source.

Category published rerun vertical D11 D11, D11s diagonal D24, D25, D28 D28, D28s mosaic none D45, D45s cross D52 D52, D52s

Different methods per source. The two sources can hold different methods for one dataset: for D52, one under published and eight under rerun. mtb.results_coverage(category) lists what each holds.

Same method in both. The two sources give different numbers; compare ranks, not decimals.

Failed re-run rows. A re-run row with an ARI near 0, where the published table scored the same method well, triggers mtb.DegenerateRerunWarning. The warning names the row and the line that drops it.

docs.title: Clustering variants
docs.text:
clustering= selects the clustering behind the clustering metrics: "default" (Leiden), "louvain" or "kmeans". In the published tables, diagonal ships all three variants for D24, D25 and D28; vertical and cross ship default only.

Details

Re-run tables are default only. With source="rerun", every row is tagged default whatever clustering= asks for.

docs.title: Step 2, Render the scIB bubble table
docs.text:
mtb.plot.bubble draws one row per method, best on top, and one column per metric. It returns a Matplotlib Figure.

fig = mtb.plot.bubble(
    df,
    metrics=["ARI", "NMI", "ASW", "cLISI"],   # column order within each family
    title="Vertical integration, D11",
    save="d11_bubble.pdf",
)
Details

Options used most often (all of them in the reference):

  • methods=[...] keeps only these methods, before ranking.
  • order=[...] puts these methods first, in this order; the rest follow best first.
  • show_language=False hides the language chips and the L badge.
  • na="skip" silences the warning about missing metrics.

docs.title: Reading the figure
docs.text:
Circle size shows the rank within a column (bigger is better); fill shows the value (darker is higher). Each metric family starts with an Overall bar, and rows are ordered by the mean of those bars.

Details

Families. Blue columns are the dimension-reduction and clustering metrics, green columns the batch-correction metrics.

Missing metrics. A dash marks a metric not computed for that method. Its Overall averages the metrics it has; a warning names each such method.

Chips. Py / R give the method's language; ? marks a method that is not in the registry, such as your own. L marks a method that uses cell-type labels (supervised), so its scores are not comparable with the unsupervised rows.

docs.title: Individual vs. summary panels
docs.text:
aggregate="dataset" (the default) plots one dataset's values. aggregate="summary" ranks methods within each dataset, then averages the ranks across datasets.

df = mtb.load_results("vertical", dataset=["D11", "D11s"], source="rerun")
fig = mtb.plot.bubble(df, metrics=["ARI", "NMI", "ASW", "cLISI"],
                      aggregate="summary", require_complete=True,
                      title="Vertical integration, D11 + D11s")
Details

Several datasets under "dataset". Values are averaged per method, a warning says so, and the row labels carry the dataset ids.

Methods missing from a dataset. Under "summary" and the default overall="rank", such a method scores rank 0 in that dataset, which pulls it down; a warning lists them. require_complete=True keeps only methods present in every dataset.

overall=. "rank" (the bubble default) and "mean_overall" (the bar default) combine datasets differently and can order methods differently. Pass the same value to plot.bubble and plot.bar for the same order.

docs.title: Audit the numbers before drawing
docs.text:
mtb.plot.build_table takes the same selection arguments and returns the numbers behind the figure as a BubbleTable.

table = mtb.plot.build_table(df, metrics=["ARI", "NMI", "ASW", "cLISI"],
                             aggregate="summary")
table.methods   # row order, best first
table.ranks     # per-column ranks, highest = best

docs.title: Summary bars
docs.text:
mtb.plot.bar draws one bar per method with its Overall score across datasets, for one metric family.

fig = mtb.plot.bar(df, group="clustering", save="bar.pdf")
Details

Dots. With several datasets and the default overall="mean_overall", one dot per dataset sits behind each bar, so a method that is good everywhere can be told from one that wins on a single dataset.

docs.title: Add your own method
docs.text:
Score your run with mtb.evaluate, reshape it with mtb.to_long, and concatenate it with a stored table.

d11_panel.py
import pandas as pd
import multibench as mtb

bench = mtb.load_results("vertical", dataset="D11", source="rerun")
# emb: your embedding, cells x dims, in the order of the D11 labels
mine = mtb.to_long(mtb.evaluate(emb, labels=mtb.labels_for("D11")["cty"]),
                   method="MyMethod", dataset="D11", category="vertical")

both = pd.concat([bench, mine])
metrics = ["ARI", "NMI", "ASW", "cLISI"]
fig = mtb.plot.bubble(both, metrics=metrics,
                      title="Vertical integration, D11 + MyMethod",
                      save="d11_vertical.pdf")
table = mtb.plot.build_table(both, metrics=metrics)
print(table.methods.index("MyMethod") + 1)   # its row in the figure
Details

Unique names. Give your run a name the stored table does not use. Duplicate (method, dataset, metric) rows raise instead of being averaged.

Supervised methods. Add mine["needs_labels"] = True to show the L badge for a method that uses cell-type labels.

docs.title: From the shell
docs.text:
The same figure without Python, with your rows saved by mine.to_csv("mine.csv", index=False):

terminal
multibench plot bubble \
    --category vertical --dataset D11 --source rerun \
    --input mine.csv \
    --metrics ARI,NMI,ASW,cLISI \
    --out d11_vertical.pdf
Details

Options. --aggregate, --overall, --require-complete, --methods and --title match the Python keywords. --result-path DIR reads another results root.

Inputs. --input takes a long CSV or a run_all output directory and can be repeated. Alone it plots your table; with --category your rows are added to the stored table.

Bars and formats. multibench plot bar --group clustering draws the summary bars. The --out extension sets the format (.pdf, .png, ...).

docs.title: Run a method
docs.text:
mtb.run runs one method on your inputs in the method's own environment and returns its output. Install that environment first (next section). mtb.run_all runs and scores every method that fits a dataset, as in the category tutorials.

import multibench as mtb

mtb.data.fetch("D28")                  # 137 MB; skipped when already present
res = mtb.run(
    "SCALEX", "diagonal",
    inputs=mtb.inputs_for("D28", "diagonal", "SCALEX"),
    out_dir="runs/scalex_d28",
)
res.output.shape                       # (11014, 10): cells x latent dimensions
Details

What a call does. run picks the method variant that matches category and the roles in inputs, converts the inputs to the canonical .h5 format and runs the method's script with out_dir as the working directory. It then loads the output.

Paths. Relative paths are fine: run makes the inputs and out_dir absolute before it starts.

Preview. mtb.run(..., dry_run=True) returns the command line without running anything or creating files. multibench run ... --dry-run prints it for a job script; mtb.scan(...)["command"] shows it per method.

docs.title: Install the method's environment
docs.text:
Each method runs in its own Linux environment, which must be installed before the first run (on macOS and Windows only dry runs work). multibench env doctor lists what is installed and what is missing.

multibench env install --methods SCALEX --packed --run

mtb.method_info("SCALEX")["env"]                # 'scmb_torch'
mtb.env.install(["SCALEX"], dry_run=False)      # the same install from Python
Details

Missing environment. When other environments are installed, run raises OSError naming the install command before anything is written.

No environment and no conda. On such a host run cannot check and fails with FileNotFoundError for conda. Run multibench env doctor.

Prebuilt archives. --packed downloads a prebuilt environment instead of building one.

docs.title: What run returns
docs.text:
res is a RunResult. res.output is the method's main output, here the joint embedding as an array.

res.output            # numpy array, shape (11014, 10)
res.extra             # other declared outputs, keyed by filename ({} for SCALEX)
res.cmd               # the command line that ran
res.out_dir           # absolute path of the run folder

Score the embedding with the dataset's label files, then see Evaluate a run:

metrics = mtb.evaluate(res.output, labels=mtb.labels_for("D28", "diagonal", "SCALEX"),
                       category="diagonal", metrics="all")
Details

Other fields. res.method is the method id; res.stdout and res.stderr hold the method's captured output.

Failed runs. A method that exits with an error raises RuntimeError with the end of its output.

Label order. With category and method, mtb.labels_for lists the files in the order that method stacks its cells, and evaluate takes the dict as is. Without them it uses the default order: RNA before ATAC, cty1, cty2, ....

Methods with another order include uniPort (ATAC first), StabMap in cross (its reference batch first) and SMILE and MultiVI in mosaic. A wrong order gives wrong scores without an error; run_all records each method's order in summary.label_order.

Your own dict. A dict you build or reorder yourself goes in as is only in the default order; name any other order with label_order=.

Batches. With two or more label files, each cell's file is its batch for the batch metrics.

docs.title: Inputs
docs.text:
inputs maps each modality role to a file path or an in-memory AnnData. method_info(m)["supports"] lists the roles each variant expects; for a dataset folder, mtb.inputs_for builds the dict.

mtb.method_info("SCALEX")["supports"]
# [{'category': 'diagonal', 'modalities': ['rna', 'atac_gas'], 'output_kind': 'embedding',
#   'n_tunable': 0, 'needs_labels': False, 'labels': []}]

mtb.run(
    "SCALEX", "diagonal",
    inputs={"rna": "data/D28/rna.h5", "atac_gas": "data/D28/atac_gas.h5"},
    out_dir="runs/scalex_d28",
)
Details

No matching variant. Inputs whose roles match no variant raise KeyError listing the variants the method has. Rename the inputs keys to fix it.

No or several variants fit. For a method with several variants, inputs_for raises mtb.AmbiguousVariantError when the folder holds the files for none or more than one of them. Pass modalities=; ["rna", "atac"] also matches an atac_gas or atac_peak variant.

Checking files. inputs_for(..., check=True) raises when a file is missing, a matrix is transposed or a label file has the wrong number of rows.

Formats. These are converted for you (see to_canonical):

  • .h5ad files
  • .csv / .tsv (cells x features) and .loom files
  • in-memory AnnData
  • canonical .h5 files, passed through unchanged

MuData. A .h5mu path raises ValueError. Pass each modality as an AnnData (mdata["rna"]), or convert it first with mtb.io.to_canonical(src, out, mod="rna").

Disk size. The canonical matrix is stored dense, so filter to highly variable genes or informative peaks first. Converting yourself with mtb.io.to_canonical(..., dtype="float32") halves the size.

No conversion. mtb.run(..., convert=False) passes your paths to the method unchanged.

docs.title: Your own data as a dataset folder
docs.text:
mtb.io.export_dataset writes an AnnData or MuData as a dataset folder that scan, run_all and inputs_for read. mtb.describe_layout(category) prints the expected files.

import anndata as ad
a = ad.read_h5ad("my_citeseq.h5ad")     # X = RNA, obsm['protein'] = ADT
mtb.io.export_dataset(a, "data/MYCITE", rna="X", adt="obsm:protein", labels="obs:celltype")
mtb.io.export_dataset(mdata, "data/MYMULTIOME", rna="rna", atac="atac", atac_kind="peak",
                      labels="rna:celltype", category="vertical")   # from a MuData
mtb.scan("MYCITE", "vertical", data_path="data")    # files_ok / env_ok per method
Details

Batches. batch="obs:sample" writes one file per batch (rna1.h5, adt1.h5, cty1.csv, ...).

One file at a time. mtb.io.to_canonical(src, "data/MYDIAG/", modality="rna") writes one modality under its canonical filename; keep the trailing / when the folder does not exist yet. mtb.io.read_canonical reads a file back as an AnnData.

Label files. A one-column CSV: a header line x, then one label per cell, e.g. pd.Series(labels, name="x").to_csv(path, index=False).

ATAC: peaks or gene activity. Say which one the matrix holds (atac_kind=). Each method expects one of the two (method_info(m)["atac"]), and the wrong one runs without an error.

ATAC file names. With category="vertical" the file is atac.h5, whatever it holds, so write the representation the method expects. Other categories keep atac_peak.h5 / atac_gas.h5.

Checks. scan's caveat column flags an ATAC file that looks like the wrong representation. inputs_for and scan name the other ATAC file when the expected one is missing.

docs.title: GPU or CPU?
docs.text:
Most methods also run without a GPU, only slower. Six need an NVIDIA GPU: on a host without one, run refuses them with OSError before starting, and scan / run_all mark them not runnable.

>>> [m for m in mtb.list_methods() if mtb.method_info(m)["requires_gpu"]]
['scBridge', 'moETM', 'SMILE', 'sciCAN', 'UnitedNet', 'iPOLNG']
>>> mtb.method_info("scJoint")["cpu_params"]
{'use_cuda': ''}
Details

CPU switches. scJoint and scMDC use CUDA unless told otherwise. On a host without a GPU, run adds the flags in method_info(m)["cpu_params"] and prints one line to stderr. A key you pass in params wins.

Environment builds. The torch environments of the tutorial methods also come as smaller CPU-only builds, which mtb.env.install picks on a host without a GPU. See Archive flavours.

docs.title: How the environment is entered: prefix and conda modes
docs.text:
run activates the installed environment folder directly, so no conda binary is needed. When no folder exists but conda is installed, it uses conda run -n <env> instead. MULTIBENCH_RUN_MODE=conda|prefix forces one mode.

Details

Where environments live. In <envs_dir>/<env>, where multibench env install --packed --run unpacks them. envs_dir defaults to MULTIBENCH_ENVS_DIR when set; the other defaults are listed under Config.

Prefix mode. The command runs under bash -c after setting CONDA_PREFIX, putting <prefix>/bin first on PATH and sourcing <prefix>/etc/conda/activate.d/*.sh.

Forced prefix mode. MULTIBENCH_RUN_MODE=prefix with no environment folder raises OSError naming envs_dir.

docs.title: Choosing a cmd_template
docs.text:
Pass cmd_template to run the command another way, for example in a container. {cmd} stands for the built command. You then manage the environment yourself: run skips its environment check.

Explicit conda envSingularity / ApptainerRun in the current env 
mtb.run(..., cmd_template="conda run -n scmb_torch {cmd}")

mtb.run(..., cmd_template="singularity exec multibench.sif {cmd}")

mtb.run(..., cmd_template="{cmd}")   # no wrapper: the active interpreter
Details

Placement. Put {cmd} last: the rest of the template is placed in front of the command.

Method scripts. repo_path= points at your own checkout of the scMultiBench method scripts. By default the package fetches one on the first run.

docs.title: Reading other output kinds
docs.text:
res.output is a numpy array for every method. Predicted labels (Matilda, scBridge, UnitedNet, Seurat_v3) come back in res.extra as lists of strings.

Details

Kinds. method_info(m)["supports"] gives each variant's output_kind: embedding or graph.

Extra outputs. res.extra maps each extra file name to its content: an array for an embedding or a graph, a list of strings for predicted labels.

Graph methods. MIRA, scMoMaT and Seurat_WNN return a cell graph, not an embedding, so embedding metrics such as ASW do not apply to res.output.

Graph methods in run_all. It scores scMoMaT through the UMAP embedding scMoMaT also writes, and records MIRA and Seurat_WNN as RUN_OK_NO_EMBEDDING.

Next: turn a run's output into scIB metrics in Evaluate a run, then render the bubble table.

docs.title: Vertical integration
docs.text:
In [1]: Copied! 
import importlib.metadata, importlib.util, sys
if importlib.util.find_spec("multibench") is None:
    # keep the numpy / pandas this interpreter already has

def stored_sweep(dataset, methods=None):
    """The stored results for `dataset`, as the object `run_all` returns."""
    long = mtb.load_results(CATEGORY, dataset=dataset, source="rerun", methods=methods)
    recs = [{"method": m, "status": "STORED", "metrics": g.set_index("metric")["value"].to_dict()}
            for m, g in long.groupby("method")]

def stand_in(dataset, methods, stored):
    """The benchmark host's run_all outputs for `dataset`; the stored results if that download fails."""

        res = mtb.load_batch(mtb.data.fetch_outputs(dataset), methods=methods)

        print(f"stand-in: the package's stored metric table ({type(e).__name__} from fetch_outputs: {e})")

LAYOUT FOR VERTICAL:
  rna.h5 + adt.h5 (CITE-seq)  or  rna.h5 + atac.h5 (multiome)
  cty.csv        <- one label file; the cells are already matched

  (numbered files live in the same flat dir; there is no batch column)

Modality roles and the filenames they resolve to:
    rna              rna.h5      - gene expression
    adt              adt.h5      - surface protein (CITE-seq antibody-derived tags)
    atac             atac.h5     - chromatin accessibility
    atac_gas         atac.h5     - ATAC as gene-activity scores  <-- note: plain atac.h5
    atac_peak        peak.h5     - ATAC as peaks                 <-- note: peak.h5, not atac.h5
    rna1/rna2/...    rna1.h5, rna2.h5, ... - one file per batch (mosaic/cross)
    adt1/adt2/...    adt1.h5, adt2.h5, ... - one file per batch (mosaic/cross)
    cty              cty.csv     - cell-type labels, one label set (vertical)
    rna_cty / atac_cty rna_cty.csv, atac_cty.csv - one label file per modality, used when RNA and ATAC come from different cells (diagonal)
    cty1/cty2/...    cty1.csv, cty2.csv, ... - one label file per batch (mosaic/cross)

!! ATAC: the role name does not guarantee the representation.
   atac_gas resolves to atac_gas.h5 if present, otherwise FALLS BACK
   to atac.h5 - and a multiome atac.h5 usually holds peaks, not gene
   activity. Check the feature names: chr1:3094772-3095489 is a peak,
   a gene symbol is gene activity.
   atac_peak resolves to atac_peak.h5, else peak.h5.
   This matters because methods disagree (lists from the registry;
   see mtb.find_methods(atac=...) / mtb.method_info(m)['atac']):
     need GENE ACTIVITY: SCALEX/scBridge/scMDC/Matilda/VIPCCA/Portal/uniPort/sciCAN/scJoint/UnitedNet/iNMF/online_iNMF/Conos
     need PEAKS:         Multigrate/Seurat_v5/MultiVI/Cobolt/scMVP/scMM/scMoMaT/moETM/MIRA/VIMCCA/SMILE/GLUE/MultiMAP/iPOLNG/StabMap/Seurat_v3/Seurat_WNN
   Feeding the wrong one runs to completion and returns a plausible
   but WRONG embedding - no error.
   Check what you actually have before trusting a cross-dataset result.
   scan() flags the commonest trap in its `caveat` column: an atac_gas
   role that fell back to an atac.h5 whose features are chr:start-end.

MODALITY FILE FORMAT (.h5) - easiest route first:
  mtb.io.to_canonical(src, dst)   converts an .h5ad and writes
  everything below correctly. Prefer it over building the file by hand.
  For a whole dataset in one call (every modality + labels, numbered
  per batch when batch= is given):
    mtb.io.export_dataset(adata, '<data_path>/MYDATA', rna='X',
                          adt='obsm:protein', labels='obs:cell_type')
  Both store matrix/data as float64, gzip-compressed and chunked, like
  the shipped files (a 3000x2000 8%-dense matrix is ~1.5 MB on disk).

  If you do build it yourself, all three datasets are required:
    matrix/data      the matrix, stored FEATURES x CELLS
    matrix/features  one entry per feature (row of matrix/data)
    matrix/barcodes  one entry per cell    (column of matrix/data)
  e.g. 2,000 genes x 5,000 cells -> matrix/data has shape (2000, 5000),
  matrix/features has 2000 entries and matrix/barcodes has 5000.
  Note: this is the TRANSPOSE of the scanpy/AnnData convention
  (AnnData.X is cells x genes). scan() rejects a transposed file, and
  a file with only matrix/data fails with a KeyError about 'features'.
Labels are a single-column CSV: one header line (typically 'x'),
then one cell-type label per cell; the evaluator reads the first
column and skips the header.

vertical: Several modalities measured in the same cells (e.g. CITE-seq RNA+ADT, or 10x multiome RNA+ATAC). Cells are already matched.


ENVIRONMENTS
  Every method runs in its own conda env (they need mutually
  incompatible framework versions). scan() checks two gates per row -
  files_ok (the inputs are on disk, oriented and labelled) and env_ok
  (that conda env exists) - and marks a method runnable only when both
  pass, so a sweep never starts one that cannot finish.
      multibench env doctor          # what is needed / what is missing
      multibench env install --run   # build them all from lockfiles
      multibench env install --methods X --packed --run   # just one

Then:  mtb.scan('MYDATA')  ->  mtb.run_all('MYDATA', '<category>', out_dir=...)

import os
import h5py
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

def subsample_dataset(src_dir, dst_dir, frac=0.6, seed=0, max_cells=2000, max_features=5000):
    """Copy a dataset under a new name, keeping a random `frac` of its cells; files with the same cell count keep the same cells."""
    rng = np.random.default_rng(seed)
    os.makedirs(dst_dir, exist_ok=True)
    counts, keep = {}, {}
    for fn in sorted(os.listdir(src_dir)):
        p = os.path.join(src_dir, fn)
        if fn.endswith(".h5"):
            with h5py.File(p) as f:
                if "matrix/data" in f:
                    counts[fn] = f["matrix/data"].shape[1]   # features x cells
        elif fn.endswith(".csv"):
            counts[fn] = len(pd.read_csv(p))
    for n in set(counts.values()):
        k = min(max(50, int(n * frac)), max_cells)
        keep[n] = np.sort(rng.choice(n, size=k, replace=False))
    for fn, n in counts.items():
        sp, dp = os.path.join(src_dir, fn), os.path.join(dst_dir, fn)
        idx = keep[n]
        if fn.endswith(".csv"):
            pd.read_csv(sp).iloc[idx].to_csv(dp, index=False)
        else:
            with h5py.File(sp) as f, h5py.File(dp, "w") as g:
                grp = g.create_group("matrix")
                n_feat = f["matrix/data"].shape[0]
                fidx = np.arange(n_feat) if n_feat <= max_features else np.sort(rng.choice(n_feat, size=max_features, replace=False))
                block = f["matrix/data"][fidx, :] if n_feat > max_features else f["matrix/data"][()]
                grp.create_dataset("data", data=np.asarray(block)[:, idx])
                if "matrix/features" in f:
                    grp.create_dataset("features", data=np.asarray(f["matrix/features"])[fidx])
                if "matrix/barcodes" in f:
                    grp.create_dataset("barcodes", data=np.asarray(f["matrix/barcodes"])[idx])
    return dst_dir

docs.title: Vertical integration¶
docs.text: Vertical integration combines modalities measured in the same cells (here CITE-seq: RNA + surface protein). Reference dataset: D11 (2,864 cells).

docs.title: 1. Install¶
docs.text:
pip install multibench-sc is all this notebook needs. Methods run in their own environments, downloaded only when you set INSTALL_ENVS = True (Linux or Colab).

Details

Default. With INSTALL_ENVS = False no environment is downloaded, only the reference data and stand-in outputs. Every cell runs; a method cell uses those outputs instead.

Running methods. Set INSTALL_ENVS = True on Colab or a Linux machine to download the prebuilt environments (no conda needed) and run the methods.

On Colab, choose a GPU runtime first (Runtime -> Change runtime type -> T4 GPU). On a CPU runtime the smaller CPU builds are installed and training methods are much slower.

docs.title: Environments - only if you will run methods¶
docs.text:
Installs the environments for Matilda, sciPENN and scMM (3 envs, 1.5 GB to download on a CPU host, 6.2 GB on a GPU host). The cell skips the download unless INSTALL_ENVS = True on Linux.

Details

Location. Environments are unpacked under mtb.config.DEFAULT.envs_dir (~/.cache/multibench/envs on a host without conda); set it before this cell to use another disk. Environments already there are skipped.

All vertical methods. multibench env install --category vertical --packed --run installs every vertical environment (18 envs, 48.1 GB to download on a CPU host, 56.4 GB on a GPU host); multibench env plan --category vertical lists the size of each.

docs.title: Run the methods¶
docs.text:
run_all runs Matilda, sciPENN and scMM on D11, each in its own environment, and scores each embedding with scIB metrics. Without environments, the cell prints one line and loads stand-in results.

Details

Stand-in. When none of these environments is installed, the cell downloads the benchmark host's run_all outputs for D11 with mtb.data.fetch_outputs (embeddings and run times included) and reloads them with mtb.load_batch.

Offline fallback. If that download fails, the cell uses the stored results (load_results(source="rerun")): status reads STORED, and there is no embedding to score.

Parameters. params={"Matilda": {"epochs": 5}} runs Matilda with epochs 5 instead of its default 30.

docs.title: Score one embedding¶
docs.text:
run_all has already scored every method. To score one embedding yourself, pass the file the method wrote and the dataset's label files to mtb.evaluate:

Details

Label order. label_order= passes the order in which the method stacked its cells, taken from the run record's labels_used.

Choosing metrics. metrics= accepts:

  • None (the default): every applicable metric
  • "clustering", "batch" or "all": a family
  • a list such as ["ARI", "NMI"]: those metrics

Batch metrics need batch= or several label files.

docs.title: Plot¶
docs.text:
res.plot() draws a bubble table. Circle size is the method's rank in each column (largest = best); colour is the metric value, scaled within the column (darker = higher).

Details

Columns. Metrics are grouped by family: blue for dimension reduction and clustering, green for batch correction. Each family starts with an Overall bar; its length and colour both show the family score.

docs.title: 3. Your own data¶
docs.text: The same calls on a dataset folder the package has not seen. describe_layout prints the files a vertical dataset needs and their format:

docs.title: 4. Stored results¶
docs.text:
The package ships stored results for 13 methods on D11 (source="rerun"). load_results reads them as a long table and mtb.plot.bubble draws it; nothing is run.

Details: sources

Two sources. For D11, the published table holds 6 methods and the package's own runs ("rerun") hold 13. load_results defaults to source="published", so every call here names its source. Where both hold a method, the values can differ.

Your own runs. run_all saves its results in out_dir; mtb.load_batch(out_dir) reloads them later without running anything.

docs.title: What runs on a dataset, and why not¶
docs.text:
scan on D11, nothing run: the first table lists the variants whose data fits, with the install command for any missing environment (env_reason); the second, why the other variants do not fit.

Details

From the shell. multibench scan D11 --category vertical prints the scan for every variant; --columns all adds every column, including command, the exact command run would execute.

docs.title: Tuning¶
docs.text:
The table counts the hyperparameters each variant exposes. mtb.params_for(method, CATEGORY, modalities) lists them; run_all(..., params={"Method": {"key": value}}) sets them.

Details

None exposed. Many upstream scripts set their hyperparameters in code; their variants accept no params.

From the shell. multibench params METHOD prints the table; multibench run-all ... --param METHOD:KEY=VALUE sets a value.

docs.title: A method's record and citation¶
docs.text:
method_info returns what the registry holds about a method, including its reference and repository; mtb.cite returns the citations for the benchmark and the methods you ran.

Details

needs_labels is True when any variant needs cell-type labels; each entry of supports gives it per variant.

verbose=True adds the long notes.

docs.title: The metrics¶
docs.text:
Two families; higher is better for every metric.

family metrics measures clustering / bio-conservation ARI, NMI, ASW, iASW, iF1, cLISI whether the embedding separates the annotated cell types batch correction ASW_batch, GC, iLISI (+ opt-in kBET) whether the batches mix within each cell type Details

Range. All lie in [0, 1] except ARI, which can be slightly negative.

Batch metrics appear only when the dataset has more than one batch.

kBET is computed only when named (metrics=["ASW_batch", "GC", "iLISI", "kBET"]); it is much slower than the others.

docs.title: Methods from the benchmark study¶
docs.text: The cell compares the methods the scMultiBench study benchmarked for vertical integration with the methods this package has a vertical variant for, and prints each missing method with the categories it has variants for.

docs.title: Troubleshooting¶
docs.text:
When a method is not runnable, scan's reason column says why; when a run fails, res.failures holds the error.

Details symptom fix files_ok False: input files not found the reason names the missing file and lists what the folder holds env_ok False run the multibench env install ... command in the reason ... which is cells x features the matrix is transposed: re-export with mtb.io.to_canonical or export_dataset a method fails res.failures.iloc[0]["error"] ends with the method's stderr a method times out raise timeout= in run_all low label_order_confidence several label files fit the cell count: check label_order_candidates in res.results batch metrics use the wrong batches res.rescore(batch=my_vector) re-scores without re-running

docs.title: Next steps¶
docs.text:
• the other tutorials: diagonal, mosaic, cross
  • the interactive explorer: the full benchmark's rankings, no install needed
  • mtb.recommend(CATEGORY, modalities=[...]): a ranking of methods from the stored results
  • mtb.sweep(...): one method over a range of values of one hyperparameter
